```{r tests}
            sample = s, revenge_scoring = REV_SCORING[[rv]], rival = RIVALS[[h]],
            rv_key = rv, rival_key = h,
            dep_cor(x$punit, x[[rv]], x[[h]]),
            status = status_of(rv, h, s, "A"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
  }))
}))
# GUARDS against the exports: each r, the correlation between the two scores,
# the difference, both ends of Zou's interval and Z, each to 1e-8 relative to
# its own size (same_each()), and the one-sided p on its own (same_p()). The
# exports hold cocor's one-sided p, 1 - pnorm(Z), which loses digits to
# cancellation when p is small and underflows to exactly 0 once Z passes about
# 8.3 (revenge against just deserts, Z = 8.70). same_p() is therefore run with
# a floor of 1e-15, which absorbs that cancellation and nothing larger: where
# the export's p is not 0 it must still agree to about 1e-8 relative (a
# doubled p fails), and where it is 0 the guard on Z carries the check.
tA <- function(s, rv, h) tests_a[tests_a$sample == s & tests_a$rv_key == rv & tests_a$rival_key == h, ]
chk_dep <- function(row, ex, what) {
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1, nrow(ex) == 1, row$n == ex$n)
  same_each(c(row$r_revenge, row$r_rival, row$r_revenge_rival, row$diff,
              row$diff_lower, row$diff_upper, row$z),
            c(ex$r_jk, ex$r_jh, ex$r_kh, ex$diff, ex$diff_lower, ex$diff_upper, ex$z), what,
            labels = c("r revenge", "r rival", "r revenge-rival", "difference",
                       "difference lower", "difference upper", "Z"))
  same_p(row$p_one, ex$p, paste(what, "one-sided p"), floor = 1e-15)
}
h10 <- read_s2("PAPER_H10"); jd10 <- read_s2("PAPER_JD_H10")
h11 <- read_s2("PAPER_H11_H10"); jd11 <- read_s2("PAPER_JD_H11_H10")
SIX <- "Punitiveness (six components)"
REG <- "one-sided, registered direction"
chk_dep(tA("Whole sample", "revenge", "desert_theory"),
        h10[h10$punitiveness == SIX & h10$sidedness == REG, ], "H10, revenge vs desert theory")
chk_dep(tA("Whole sample", "revenge", "just_deserts"),
        jd10[jd10$punitiveness == SIX & jd10$sidedness == REG, ], "H10, revenge vs just deserts")
chk_dep(tA("Whole sample", "revenge3", "desert_theory"),
        h10[h10$punitiveness == SIX & grepl("^one-sided.*three-item", h10$sidedness), ],
        "H10, three-item revenge vs desert theory")
chk_dep(tA("Retributivists", "revenge", "desert_theory"),
        h11[h11$punitiveness == SIX & h11$sidedness == REG, ], "H11, revenge vs desert theory")
chk_dep(tA("Retributivists", "revenge", "just_deserts"),
        jd11[jd11$punitiveness == SIX & jd11$sidedness == REG, ], "H11, revenge vs just deserts")
# GUARDS against the paper's printed values (Part 2 and Part 3) and, for the
# new comparison (revenge vs severity-deserts), against its values computed
# independently of this document.
a <- tA("Whole sample", "revenge", "desert_theory")
paper_same(a$diff, .002, 3, "H10 dt: diff .002"); paper_same(a$diff_lower, -.039, 3, "H10 dt: lower")
paper_same(a$diff_upper, .042, 3, "H10 dt: upper"); paper_same(a$z, 0.09, 2, "H10 dt: Z 0.09")
paper_same(a$p_one, .47, 2, "H10 dt: one-sided p .47")
a <- tA("Whole sample", "revenge", "just_deserts")
paper_same(a$diff, .244, 3, "H10 jd: diff .244"); paper_same(a$diff_lower, .188, 3, "H10 jd: lower")
paper_same(a$diff_upper, .301, 3, "H10 jd: upper"); paper_same(a$z, 8.70, 2, "H10 jd: Z 8.70")
a <- tA("Whole sample", "revenge", "severity_deserts")
paper_same(a$diff, -.058, 3, "revenge vs severity-deserts: diff -.058 (new; computed independently)")
paper_same(a$diff_lower, -.094, 3, "revenge vs severity-deserts: lower -.094")
paper_same(a$diff_upper, -.022, 3, "revenge vs severity-deserts: upper -.022")
paper_same(a$z, -3.20, 2, "revenge vs severity-deserts: Z -3.20")
a <- tA("Retributivists", "revenge", "desert_theory")
paper_same(a$diff, .026, 3, "H11 dt: diff .026"); paper_same(a$diff_lower, -.060, 3, "H11 dt: lower")
paper_same(a$diff_upper, .112, 3, "H11 dt: upper"); paper_same(a$p_one, .28, 2, "H11 dt: p .28")
a <- tA("Retributivists", "revenge", "just_deserts")
paper_same(a$diff, .414, 3, "H11 jd: diff .414"); paper_same(a$diff_lower, .295, 3, "H11 jd: lower")
paper_same(a$diff_upper, .531, 3, "H11 jd: upper"); paper_same(a$z, 6.75, 2, "H11 jd: Z 6.75")

# --- B. Paired endorsement --------------------------------------------------------
# Four-item revenge only: H9 is registered on the four items, and the
# three-item check concerns H10's correlations, not endorsement.
tests_b <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(SAMPLES), function(s) {
  x <- SAMPLES[[s]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(RIVALS), function(h) {
    cbind(family = "Endorsement: rival minus revenge (paired t, paired d)",
          sample = s, revenge_scoring = REV_SCORING[["revenge"]], rival = RIVALS[[h]],
          rv_key = "revenge", rival_key = h,
          paired_diff(x[[h]], x$revenge),
          status = status_of("revenge", h, s, "B"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))
tB <- function(s, h) tests_b[tests_b$sample == s & tests_b$rival_key == h, ]
# GUARDS against the H9 exports: every number to 1e-8 relative to its own
# size (same_each()), and both p's on their own (same_p(); no floor, because
# 01 and this document both take them from t.test()).
chk_pair <- function(row, ex, what) {
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1, nrow(ex) == 1, row$n == ex$n)
  same_each(c(row$M1, row$M2, row$mean_diff, row$diff_lower, row$diff_upper, row$t,
              row$d, row$d_lower, row$d_upper),
            c(ex$M1, ex$M2, ex$mean_diff, ex$ci_lower, ex$ci_upper, ex$t,
              ex$d, ex$d_lower, ex$d_upper), what,
            labels = c("M rival", "M revenge", "difference", "difference lower",
                       "difference upper", "t", "d", "d lower", "d upper"))
  same_p(row$p_two, ex$p_two, paste(what, "two-sided p"))
  same_p(row$p_one, ex$p_dir, paste(what, "one-sided p"))
}
h11_9 <- read_s2("PAPER_H11_H9"); jd11_9 <- read_s2("PAPER_JD_H11_H9")
chk_pair(tB("Whole sample", "desert_theory"), h9, "H9, desert theory vs revenge")
chk_pair(tB("Whole sample", "just_deserts"), jd9[jd9$var1 == "just_deserts", ],
         "H9, just deserts vs revenge")
chk_pair(tB("Retributivists", "desert_theory"), h11_9, "H11 (H9), desert theory vs revenge")
chk_pair(tB("Retributivists", "just_deserts"), jd11_9[jd11_9$var1 == "just_deserts", ],
         "H11 (H9), just deserts vs revenge")
b <- tB("Whole sample", "desert_theory")
paper_same(b$mean_diff, 1.46, 2, "H9: difference 1.46"); paper_same(b$diff_lower, 1.38, 2, "H9: lower")
paper_same(b$diff_upper, 1.54, 2, "H9: upper"); paper_same(b$t, 36.22, 2, "H9: t 36.22")
paper_same(b$d, 1.18, 2, "H9: d 1.18"); paper_same(b$d_lower, 1.09, 2, "H9: d lower")
paper_same(b$d_upper, 1.26, 2, "H9: d upper")
b <- tB("Whole sample", "just_deserts")
paper_same(b$mean_diff, 1.52, 2, "H9 jd: difference 1.52"); paper_same(b$t, 33.27, 2, "H9 jd: t")
paper_same(b$d, 1.08, 2, "H9 jd: d 1.08")
paper_same(tB("Retributivists", "desert_theory")$d, 1.25, 2, "H11: H9 d 1.25")
paper_same(tB("Retributivists", "just_deserts")$d, 0.93, 2, "H11: H9 jd d 0.93")

# One table, family A and family B stacked; columns a family does not use are
# NA. The statistic column says which test statistic each row carries.
# ONE-SIDED p ONLY WHERE A REGISTERED DIRECTION EXISTS. The paper's rule is
# that analyses that were not registered are two-sided unless they rerun a
# registered test (Analytic Strategy). Severity-deserts reruns none, so its
# rows carry the two-sided p only and the one-sided column is NA. Printing a
# "registered-direction" p there would invite misreading: revenge against
# severity-deserts gives two-sided p = .0014 with severity-deserts AHEAD, which
# a one-sided p of .9993 would hide.
one_sided_or_na <- function(p, rival_key) ifelse(rival_key == "severity_deserts", NA_real_, p)
TEST_COLS <- c("family", "sample", "revenge_scoring", "rival", "n",
               "r_revenge", "r_rival", "r_revenge_rival",
               "M_rival", "M_revenge", "difference", "difference_lower", "difference_upper",
               "statistic", "statistic_value", "df", "p_two_sided",
               "p_one_sided_registered_direction", "paired_d", "paired_d_lower",
               "paired_d_upper", "status")
out_a <- data.frame(tests_a[, c("family", "sample", "revenge_scoring", "rival", "n",
                                "r_revenge", "r_rival", "r_revenge_rival")],
                    M_rival = NA_real_, M_revenge = NA_real_,
                    difference = tests_a$diff, difference_lower = tests_a$diff_lower,
                    difference_upper = tests_a$diff_upper,
                    statistic = "Steiger Z", statistic_value = tests_a$z, df = NA_real_,
                    p_two_sided = tests_a$p_two,
                    p_one_sided_registered_direction = one_sided_or_na(tests_a$p_one,
                                                                       tests_a$rival_key),
                    paired_d = NA_real_, paired_d_lower = NA_real_, paired_d_upper = NA_real_,
                    status = tests_a$status, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
out_b <- data.frame(tests_b[, c("family", "sample", "revenge_scoring", "rival", "n")],
                    r_revenge = NA_real_, r_rival = NA_real_, r_revenge_rival = NA_real_,
                    M_rival = tests_b$M1, M_revenge = tests_b$M2,
                    difference = tests_b$mean_diff, difference_lower = tests_b$diff_lower,
                    difference_upper = tests_b$diff_upper,
                    statistic = "paired t", statistic_value = tests_b$t, df = tests_b$df,
                    p_two_sided = tests_b$p_two,
                    p_one_sided_registered_direction = one_sided_or_na(tests_b$p_one,
                                                                       tests_b$rival_key),
                    paired_d = tests_b$d, paired_d_lower = tests_b$d_lower,
                    paired_d_upper = tests_b$d_upper,
                    status = tests_b$status, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
TESTS <- rbind(out_a[, TEST_COLS], out_b[, TEST_COLS])
rownames(TESTS) <- NULL
# GUARDS on the table's labelling: the one-sided p is blank on every
# severity-deserts row and on no other; every row has a two-sided p; and no
# row calls itself "registered test" (see WHAT IS REGISTERED above).
sev <- TESTS$rival == "Severity-deserts"
stopifnot(sum(sev) == 6,
          all(is.na(TESTS$p_one_sided_registered_direction[sev])),
          !anyNA(TESTS$p_one_sided_registered_direction[!sev]),
          !anyNA(TESTS$p_two_sided),
          !any(grepl("registered test (", TESTS$status, fixed = TRUE)),
          !any(grepl("^registered test", TESTS$status)))
print(TESTS[, c("sample", "revenge_scoring", "rival", "difference", "difference_lower",
                "difference_upper", "statistic_value", "p_two_sided", "paired_d")], digits = 3)
```

# 5. Two models of agency

```{r fig05_agency, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 5: TWO MODELS OF AGENCY (BAR CHART OF COHEN'S d, TWO GROUPS) ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: Cohen's d, retributivists (371) minus the participants
# who ranked deterrence or incapacitation first (453), for seven registered
# contrasts, grouped under the two models of agency Dan proposed:
#   AGENCY AS BLAMEWORTHINESS: agency and the capacity to choose make the
#     offender the author of the crime, so a retributivist who holds this view
#     should see offenders as criminal to the core (essentialism), see crime as
#     a choice, and reject society's share of responsibility. The model
#     predicts that retributivists score HIGHER on all three.
#   AGENCY AS BENEVOLENCE: retribution rests on respect for the offender's
#     dignity as an agent, so a retributivist who holds this view should be no
#     more hateful and no more willing to degrade, to inflict suffering, or to
#     impose harsh prison conditions. The model predicts that retributivists
#     score NO HIGHER (or lower) on all four.
# The d values and intervals are read from the export and each is recomputed
# from the data exactly as 01 computes it.
# READS: sc; PAPER_contrasts_vs_deter_incap.
# WRITES: pt_05_agency; its values.
# MATCHES: Results, Part 3 and General Discussion (essentialism d = 0.59,
#          choice 0.47, rejecting society's responsibility 0.50); Table S19,
#          last column (hatred 0.48, degradation 0.36, suffering 0.42, harsh
#          conditions 0.52). The contrasts are registered (H13, H16, H17, H19);
#          the comparison group (leaving out the rehabilitation-first) and the
#          grouping into two models are not.
# A backup slide: slide 10, in the main line, tells the same comparison in
# shares. The caption says that the seven contrasts are preregistered, under
# which hypotheses, and that only the comparison group and the two-model
# grouping are not; a guard checks the hypotheses against the export.
MODELS <- c(blame = "Agency as blameworthiness: predicts retributivists higher",
            benev = "Agency as benevolence: predicts retributivists no higher")
AGENCY <- data.frame(
  variable = c("essentialism", "choice", "society_reject",
               "hatred", "degradation", "suffering", "harsh"),
  label = c("Essentialism about offenders", "Crime is a choice",
            "Rejecting society’s responsibility",
            "Hatred of offenders", "Degradation of prisoners",
            "Infliction of suffering", "Harsh prison conditions"),
  model = MODELS[c("blame", "blame", "blame", "benev", "benev", "benev", "benev")],
  # The d the paper prints for each (two decimals), for the printed-value guard.
  paper_d = c(0.59, 0.47, 0.50, 0.48, 0.36, 0.42, 0.52),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cq <- read_s2("PAPER_contrasts_vs_deter_incap")
stopifnot(all(AGENCY$variable %in% cq$variable), all(cq$grouping == "grp_vs_deter_incap"))
ag <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(AGENCY)), function(i) {
  ex <- cq[cq$variable == AGENCY$variable[i], ]
  stopifnot(nrow(ex) == 1, ex$alternative == "greater")
  # GUARD: recompute the contrast from the data, 01's way (welch_d(), which is
  # welch_contrast()), and demand the export's n's exactly; its means, t, d
  # and interval each to 1e-8 relative to its own size (same_each()); and its
  # one-sided p on its own, to 1e-8 relative (same_p()), because inside one
  # vector beside t and the means a p of 1e-12 would hardly be checked.
  re <- welch_d(d[[AGENCY$variable[i]]], sc$grp_vs_deter_incap, alternative = "greater")
  stopifnot(re$n1 == ex$n1, re$n2 == ex$n2)
  same_each(c(re$M1, re$M2, re$t, re$d, re$lower, re$upper),
            c(ex$M1, ex$M2, ex$t, ex$d, ex$d_lower, ex$d_upper),
            paste("slide 5: contrast,", AGENCY$variable[i]),
            labels = c("M1", "M2", "t", "d", "d lower", "d upper"))
  same_p(re$p_dir, ex$p_dir, paste("slide 5: one-sided p,", AGENCY$variable[i]))
  paper_same(ex$d, AGENCY$paper_d[i], 2, paste("slide 5: printed d,", AGENCY$variable[i]))
  data.frame(label = AGENCY$label[i], model = AGENCY$model[i], d = ex$d,
             lower = ex$d_lower, upper = ex$d_upper, p_dir = ex$p_dir,
             n1 = ex$n1, n2 = ex$n2, hypothesis = ex$hypothesis,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
# Every one of the seven is one-sided p < .001 (Table S19 note).
stopifnot(all(ag$p_dir < .001), all(ag$n1 == 371), all(ag$n2 == 453))
# GUARD FOR THE CAPTION: the caption names the hypotheses the seven contrasts
# were registered under, H13 (the four hostile measures), H16 (essentialism),
# H17 (choice) and H19 (society's responsibility), read here from the export,
# so the caption cannot name a hypothesis the contrasts do not belong to.
stopifnot(identical(sort(unique(ag$hypothesis)), c("H13", "H16", "H17", "H19")),
          identical(ag$hypothesis[ag$label %in% AGENCY$label[4:7]], rep("H13", 4)))

# Rows keep the order listed above within each group; rows are drawn
# bottom-up, so the levels are reversed. The facet order puts the
# blameworthiness group on top.
ag$label <- factor(ag$label, levels = rev(AGENCY$label))
ag$model <- factor(ag$model, levels = unname(MODELS))
# The two groups take two clearly different grays; the strip above each panel
# names the group and its prediction, so no legend is needed.
# DANGER: not the lightest data gray (G4). On slide 6, G4 means "one-sided
# p >= .05", and every benevolence contrast here is p < .001; in G4 these
# bars would look weak or non-significant, the opposite of what they show.
# G3 keeps the two groups clearly apart (#1a1a1a against #737373).
MODEL_FILLS <- setNames(c(G1, G3), unname(MODELS))
fig05 <- bar_d(ag, "label", "model", fills = MODEL_FILLS,
               xlim = c(0, 0.8), xbreaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.2),
               # "95% CI" sits in the axis title, which frees the caption's
               # two lines for the comparison group and what was registered.
               xlab = "Retributivists minus deterrence- or incapacitation-first (Cohen’s d, 95% CI)") +
  # ONE PANEL PER MODEL, stacked, each only as tall as its rows need
  # (space = "free_y"), so the bars are equally thick in both panels.
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.text = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", colour = INK, hjust = 0,
                                  margin = margin(t = 6, b = 8)),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(1.4, "lines")) +
  labs(title = "Two Models of Agency",
       # "n\u00a0=\u00a0371" uses non-breaking spaces, so the caption's line wrap
       # can never split a sample size from its "n =".
       # WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT REGISTERED, said on the slide, as the paper says
       # it wherever these d's appear (Part 3, Figure 10 note). The caption
       # first says what WAS registered, the seven contrasts and their
       # hypotheses (guarded above), and then that ONLY the comparison group
       # and the grouping into two models were not, so no one reads the whole
       # slide as exploratory. That the comparison leaves out the 124 who
       # ranked rehabilitation first is said by the two group sizes, which do
       # not add to 948, and by the header of this chunk; the caption keeps to
       # two lines.
       caption = cap("Retributivists (ranked retribution first, n\u00a0=\u00a0371) vs deterrence- or incapacitation-first (n\u00a0=\u00a0453). Positive d: retributivists higher.",
                     "The seven contrasts are preregistered (H13, H16, H17, H19); only this comparison group and the two-model grouping are not."))
save_slide(fig05, "pt_05_agency")
keep_values("pt_05_agency", data.frame(
  label = paste0(sub(":.*", "", ag$model), ": ", ag$label, " (d, 371 vs 453)"),
  value = ag$d, lower = ag$lower, upper = ag$upper, n = ag$n1 + ag$n2))
fig05
```

# 6. The four ways of identifying retributivists

```{r fig06_four_groupings, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 6: THE REGISTERED CONTRASTS UNDER EACH OF THE FOUR GROUPINGS ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: Cohen's d with its 95% interval for the 20 registered
# contrasts (H13 to H21), under each registered grouping, as four panels side
# by side that share one list of measures:
#   Ranking        retribution ranked first (371) against all others (577),
#                  the registered primary comparison;
#   Median split   on relative retribution (470 against 478);
#   Thirds         top against bottom third of relative retribution (314, 317);
#   Sentencing ratio  kept or raised the sentence (514) against reduced it (433).
# The 20 contrasts are the 19 rows from the hostile aggression cluster to
# convicting on uncertain evidence, plus punitiveness counted once: the
# six-component score under the first three groupings, and under the
# sentencing ratio the five attitude components without the sentence, because
# that grouping is built from the sentences (prereg 5.11; Table S16 note). The
# first sentence (H14) cannot be run under the ratio and is marked "not run".
# The exploratory E1 rows and the second punitiveness row are left out, as
# the paper's counts leave them out.
# READS: sc, d; PAPER_contrasts_rank, _med, _tert, _ratio; PAPER_scorecard
#        (for the guard on the medians).
# WRITES: pt_06_four_groupings; its values, with each panel's median d and
#         its typical interval half-width.
# MATCHES: Table S16 (all four columns, and the medians 0.51, 0.20, 0.30,
#          0.40); Supplement S5.
# DESIGN (slide 6 is in the talk's main line):
#   - NO ERROR BARS. With 79 bars on one slide, whiskers would crowd the bars.
#     Every interval here is nearly the same width within a grouping (the
#     groups' sizes do not change from one measure to the next), so the
#     caption states the typical half-width, computed below from the exports,
#     and the values table keeps every interval.
#   - The first panel is headed "Ranking (vs all others)", which says on the
#     slide that the registered comparison is with all 577 others, not with
#     the 453 of slide 5.
#   - A dashed line at each panel's median d, labelled with its value, so the
#     medians of slide 7 can be read here without it.
#   - Row labels at 17 pt, large enough to read on a projector, and no
#     legend: the caption says what the dark bars are, and the legend's
#     height goes to the rows.
#   - The ratio's empty first-sentence cell reads "not run", and the caption
#     says why.
GROUPINGS <- data.frame(
  key = c("rank", "med", "tert", "ratio"),
  col = c("grp_rank", "grp_med", "grp_tert", "grp_ratio"),
  name = c("Ranking", "Median split", "Top vs bottom third", "Sentencing ratio"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# The 19 non-punitiveness contrasts, by their variable names in the exports and
# the scored data, with the labels the slide prints (Table S16's wording, except
# "Hatred of offenders", which is slide 5's label for the same measure, so the
# two slides name it alike).
CONTRASTS <- c(hostile_agg = "Hostile aggression cluster", hatred = "Hatred of offenders",
               revenge = "Revenge", degradation = "Degradation of prisoners",
               suffering = "Infliction of suffering",
               prisonviol = "Tolerance of prison violence", anger = "Anger",
               exclusion = "Social exclusion", harsh = "Harsh prison conditions",
               crimerates = "Perceived crime rates", fear = "Fear of crime",
               Sentence1_z = "First sentence", Shark_3 = "Painful death for the shark",
               essentialism = "Essentialism about offenders", choice = "Crime is a choice",
               leanPros = "Leaning toward the prosecution",
               society_reject = "Rejecting society’s responsibility",
               dueprocess = "Due-process permissiveness",
               uncertain = "Convicting on uncertain evidence")
PUNIT_LAB <- "Punitiveness"
# Punitiveness under each grouping: the export's variable name and the
# person-score column that holds it.
# DANGER: under the ratio this must stay the five-component score. The
# six-component score contains the first sentence, and the ratio grouping is
# built from the sentences, so using it there would put the sentence on both
# sides of the comparison.
PUNIT_VAR <- c(rank = "punit_parts6", med = "punit_parts6", tert = "punit_parts6",
               ratio = "punit_parts5z")
PUNIT_COL <- c(punit_parts6 = "punit_six", punit_parts5z = "punit_five_z")

g6 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(GROUPINGS)), function(k) {
  gk <- GROUPINGS[k, ]
  ex <- read_s2(paste0("PAPER_contrasts_", gk$key))
  stopifnot(all(ex$grouping == gk$col))
  vars <- c(names(CONTRASTS), PUNIT_VAR[[gk$key]])
  # H14 (the first sentence) is absent from the ratio export by design.
  if (gk$key == "ratio") {
    stopifnot(!"Sentence1_z" %in% ex$variable, !"punit_parts6" %in% ex$variable)
    vars <- setdiff(vars, "Sentence1_z")
  }
  do.call(rbind, lapply(vars, function(v) {
    e <- ex[ex$variable == v, ]
    stopifnot(nrow(e) == 1, e$alternative == "greater",
              e$hypothesis %in% paste0("H", 13:21))
    # GUARD: recompute from the data, 01's way, and demand the export: t, d
    # and both ends of the interval each to 1e-8 relative to its own size
    # (same_each(); a d of 0.00 beside a t of 7 would otherwise hardly be
    # checked), and the one-sided p on its own (same_p()). The p matters here:
    # it sets each bar's shade and slide 7's counts.
    y <- if (v %in% names(PUNIT_COL)) ps[[PUNIT_COL[[v]]]] else d[[v]]
    re <- welch_d(y, sc[[gk$col]], alternative = "greater")
    stopifnot(re$n1 == e$n1, re$n2 == e$n2)
    same_each(c(re$t, re$d, re$lower, re$upper), c(e$t, e$d, e$d_lower, e$d_upper),
              paste("slide 6:", gk$key, v), labels = c("t", "d", "d lower", "d upper"))
    same_p(re$p_dir, e$p_dir, paste("slide 6: one-sided p,", gk$key, v))
    data.frame(grouping = gk$key, variable = v,
               label = if (v %in% names(PUNIT_COL)) PUNIT_LAB else CONTRASTS[[v]],
               d = e$d, lower = e$d_lower, upper = e$d_upper, p_dir = e$p_dir,
               n1 = e$n1, n2 = e$n2, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))
# GUARDS: 20 contrasts under each grouping but the ratio, 19 under it.
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(table(factor(g6$grouping, levels = GROUPINGS$key))),
                    c(20L, 20L, 20L, 19L)))
# GUARDS against Table S16 (two decimals), a few values per column, so a
# column cannot be misassigned: punitiveness, essentialism, the shark's pain
# (negative under three groupings), and fear of crime.
gd <- function(g, v) g6$d[g6$grouping == g & g6$variable == v]
paper_same(gd("rank", "punit_parts6"), 0.80, 2, "S16: punitiveness, ranking")
paper_same(gd("med", "punit_parts6"), 0.24, 2, "S16: punitiveness, median split")
paper_same(gd("tert", "punit_parts6"), 0.36, 2, "S16: punitiveness, thirds")
paper_same(gd("ratio", "punit_parts5z"), 0.61, 2, "S16: punitiveness, ratio")
paper_same(gd("rank", "essentialism"), 0.69, 2, "S16: essentialism, ranking")
paper_same(gd("ratio", "essentialism"), 0.48, 2, "S16: essentialism, ratio")
paper_same(gd("med", "Shark_3"), -0.04, 2, "S16: shark, median split")
paper_same(gd("tert", "Shark_3"), -0.11, 2, "S16: shark, thirds")
paper_same(gd("ratio", "Shark_3"), -0.06, 2, "S16: shark, ratio")
paper_same(gd("tert", "fear"), 0.08, 2, "S16: fear, thirds")

# Panel titles carry each grouping's two group sizes, read from the data.
ns6 <- aggregate(cbind(n1, n2) ~ grouping, data = g6, FUN = function(x) x[1])
stopifnot(all(aggregate(cbind(n1, n2) ~ grouping, data = g6,
                        FUN = function(x) length(unique(x)))[, -1] == 1))
GROUP_TITLE <- setNames(sprintf("%s\n%d vs %d", GROUPINGS$name,
                                ns6$n1[match(GROUPINGS$key, ns6$grouping)],
                                ns6$n2[match(GROUPINGS$key, ns6$grouping)]),
                        GROUPINGS$key)
# SLIDE 6'S OWN PANEL TITLES. The first panel is headed "Ranking (vs all
# others)", on its own line above the two group sizes. GROUP_TITLE itself
# keeps the plain "Ranking", because slide 7 labels its bars with it and has
# its own caption for the comparison.
# DANGER: slide 6 must use GROUP_TITLE6 everywhere (the panels, the "not run"
# cell, the median lines); a layer given GROUP_TITLE instead would sit in a
# panel of its own, a fifth panel with a different name.
GROUP_TITLE6 <- GROUP_TITLE
GROUP_TITLE6[["rank"]] <- sub("^Ranking", "Ranking (vs all others)", GROUP_TITLE[["rank"]])
stopifnot(GROUP_TITLE6[["rank"]] == "Ranking (vs all others)\n371 vs 577",
          identical(GROUP_TITLE6[-1], GROUP_TITLE[-1]))
g6$panel <- factor(GROUP_TITLE6[g6$grouping], levels = unname(GROUP_TITLE6))
# ROW ORDER: by the size of d under the ranking, the registered primary
# grouping, largest at the top, so the first panel reads as a ranked list and
# the other three show how each measure fares when retributivists are picked
# out another way.
row_order <- g6$label[g6$grouping == "rank"][order(g6$d[g6$grouping == "rank"])]
g6$label <- factor(g6$label, levels = row_order)
# Shade: dark where the registered one-sided test reached p < .05, light where
# it did not (Table S16's dagger). These are the counts slide 7 reports.
SIG6 <- c("One-sided p < .05", "One-sided p ≥ .05")
g6$sig <- factor(ifelse(g6$p_dir < .05, SIG6[1], SIG6[2]), levels = SIG6)
FILLS6 <- setNames(c(G2, G4), SIG6)
# The significant bars are G2. The slide draws no intervals, so nothing is
# knocked out in white, but mark_dark() is run as a GUARD: it halts if a
# dark bar (a contrast significant in the registered, positive direction) were
# ever negative, which would mean a sign or a grouping had been flipped.
g6 <- mark_dark(g6, "sig", FILLS6, "d")
stopifnot(identical(g6$dark, g6$p_dir < .05))
# The blank the ratio leaves for the first sentence, marked in its own panel.
not_run <- data.frame(label = factor("First sentence", levels = row_order),
                      panel = factor(GROUP_TITLE6[["ratio"]], levels = unname(GROUP_TITLE6)))

# EACH PANEL'S MEDIAN d, drawn as a dashed line. The median is taken over the
# ABSOLUTE d's, as Table S16 and 01's scorecard take it (and as slide 7 does),
# and guarded against both. The line is drawn on the SIGNED axis, so the knit
# also demands that the signed median equals the absolute one; it does in every
# grouping (the few negative d's all fall below the middle of each list), and
# if it ever did not, the line would stand at a value no bar's median has.
scc6 <- read_s2("PAPER_scorecard")
scc6 <- scc6[scc6$row_set == "Registered (H13 to H21), punitiveness once", ]
SC_RUN6 <- c(rank = "Ranking (primary)", med = "Median split", tert = "Tertiles",
             ratio = "Sentencing ratio grouping")
med6 <- data.frame(grouping = GROUPINGS$key, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
med6$median_abs_d <- sapply(med6$grouping, function(g) median(abs(g6$d[g6$grouping == g])))
med6$median_d     <- sapply(med6$grouping, function(g) median(g6$d[g6$grouping == g]))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(med6))) {
  s <- scc6[scc6$run == SC_RUN6[[med6$grouping[i]]], ]
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1)
  same(med6$median_abs_d[i], s$median_abs_estimate, paste("slide 6: median |d|,", med6$grouping[i]))
}
same_each(med6$median_d, med6$median_abs_d, "slide 6: signed median = absolute median",
          labels = med6$grouping)
paper_same(med6$median_abs_d, c(0.51, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40), 2, "Table S16: median |d| (slide 6)")
med6$panel <- factor(GROUP_TITLE6[med6$grouping], levels = unname(GROUP_TITLE6))
# Where the line and its label sit. The rows are the 20 levels of `label`,
# at positions 1 (bottom) to 20 (top) on the discrete axis; a position given
# as a number is placed on that same axis. The line runs from below the
# bottom row to half a row above the top row, and the label sits on the end of
# the line, in the room the y axis's expansion (below) leaves over the top row.
# WHY SO LOW IN THAT ROOM: the label's bottom edge is 0.55 of a row above the
# top row, and the top row's bar ends 0.33 above it (bars are 0.66 thick), so
# about a fifth of a row (about 20 px in the PNG) separates the label from the
# bar, and about 30 px separates it from the panel headers above. Set higher,
# at the top of the band, the label sat as close under the two-line header
# as the header's lines sit to each other, and read as a third header line.
# DANGER: MED_LABEL_Y must stay above the top of the row-20 bar (20.33), or
# the label's white box cuts into the bar; and MED_LINE_TOP must stay just
# below MED_LABEL_Y, so the line ends under its label.
N_ROWS6 <- nlevels(g6$label)
stopifnot(N_ROWS6 == 20)
MED_LINE_TOP <- N_ROWS6 + 0.5
MED_LABEL_Y  <- N_ROWS6 + 0.55
stopifnot(MED_LABEL_Y > N_ROWS6 + 0.33, MED_LINE_TOP < MED_LABEL_Y)
# THE LINES AS SEGMENTS. Each panel's line runs from 0.4 (below the bottom
# row) to MED_LINE_TOP, except in the sentencing-ratio panel, where the line
# (at 0.40) would run through the "not run" label: there it stops half a row
# below the first-sentence row and starts again half a row above it, so the
# label sits in a gap of the dashed line.
NOT_RUN_Y <- as.integer(not_run$label)
med_seg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(med6)), function(i) {
  if (med6$grouping[i] == "ratio")
    data.frame(panel = med6$panel[i], x = med6$median_abs_d[i],
               y = c(0.4, NOT_RUN_Y + 0.5), yend = c(NOT_RUN_Y - 0.5, MED_LINE_TOP))
  else
    data.frame(panel = med6$panel[i], x = med6$median_abs_d[i], y = 0.4, yend = MED_LINE_TOP)
}))
stopifnot(nrow(med_seg) == 5)

# THE TYPICAL WIDTH OF THE INTERVALS, WHICH THE SLIDE DOES NOT DRAW. For each
# grouping, the median over its contrasts of the half-width of the 95%
# interval of d, (upper - lower) / 2, from the exports (the lower and upper
# columns of g6 are the exports' d_lower and d_upper, guarded above). The
# interval of d is not exactly symmetric, so the caption says "about".
# Within a grouping the half-widths hardly vary, because the two groups' sizes
# are the same for every measure; they are wider for the thirds, which compare
# 631 of the 948 participants.
hw6 <- data.frame(grouping = GROUPINGS$key, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
hw6$median_half_width <- sapply(hw6$grouping, function(g) {
  x <- g6[g6$grouping == g, ]
  median((x$upper - x$lower) / 2)
})
hw6$shown <- sprintf("%.2f", hw6$median_half_width)
# GUARD ON THE CAPTION'S FORM. The caption states one half-width for the
# ranking, the median split and the sentencing ratio, and another for the
# thirds. That form is true only if the first three round to the same two
# decimals and the thirds do not; otherwise the knit stops, and the caption
# must be rewritten. The values are computed here, not typed, so the caption
# follows the data (±0.13, and ±0.16 for the thirds).
HW_MAIN  <- unique(hw6$shown[hw6$grouping != "tert"])
HW_THIRD <- hw6$shown[hw6$grouping == "tert"]
stopifnot(length(HW_MAIN) == 1, HW_THIRD != HW_MAIN)
cat(sprintf("Slide 6: median 95%% CI half-width %s (ranking, median split, ratio), %s (thirds)\n",
            HW_MAIN, HW_THIRD))

fig06 <- ggplot(g6, aes(x = d, y = label)) +
  # THE MEDIAN LINES, dashed and black, drawn BEHIND the bars. They show in
  # the white gap between every pair of rows and past the end of every bar
  # shorter than the median, which is enough for the eye to follow each line
  # down its panel; a bar that hides the line is plainly longer than the
  # median. Drawn over the bars, the line would have to cross the dark bars
  # in white to be seen, and a white stripe through a bar cuts it in two,
  # leaving a stub past the stripe that reads as a tick or an interval's cap.
  # DANGER: this layer must come BEFORE geom_col(). Layers are drawn in the
  # order they are added; after geom_col() the line would run over the bars.
  geom_segment(data = med_seg, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = y, yend = yend),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "22") +
  # Bars 0.66 of a row thick, so the gaps between rows, where the dashed
  # lines show, are a third of a row: wide enough to carry a dash in every
  # gap.
  geom_col(aes(fill = sig), width = 0.66) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.6) +
  # The median's value above its line, at 16 pt, in the same two decimals as
  # Table S16 and slide 7. In a white box with no border: centred on a median
  # of 0.20 or 0.30 the label reaches back past zero, and the box keeps the
  # zero line (and the light gridlines) from running through the words. The
  # box sits in the empty band above the top row (MED_LABEL_Y), so it covers
  # no bar.
  geom_label(data = med6, aes(x = median_abs_d, y = MED_LABEL_Y,
                              label = paste("median", fmt_d(median_abs_d))),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = 0, size = 16 / .pt, colour = INK,
             fill = "white", label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.08, "lines"),
             label.r = unit(0, "lines")) +
  # "not run" at about 15 pt in the axis-text gray: large and dark enough to
  # read on a projector, italic so it is not mistaken for a value. The caption
  # says why the cell is empty.
  geom_text(data = not_run, aes(x = 0.03, y = label, label = "not run"),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 5.4, colour = INK2, fontface = "italic") +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = FILLS6, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.4, 0.8), labels = axis_d) +
  # ROOM ABOVE THE TOP ROW for the median labels: 1.9 row-heights at the top
  # (0.6 at the bottom, the usual margin). The labels sit low in this room
  # (MED_LABEL_Y, above), and the empty part above them is the gap that keeps
  # them from reading as part of the panel headers. DANGER: shrinking the
  # top margin pushes the labels up against the headers.
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 1.9))) +
  # Without intervals the axis needs only to hold the bars: the smallest d is
  # -0.11 (the shark's pain, thirds) and the largest 0.80 (punitiveness,
  # ranking).
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.16, 0.92), clip = "off") +
  # THE CAPTION: what the dark bars are, which way a positive d points (the
  # shark's pain points the other way under three groupings), the typical
  # half-width of the intervals (computed above), and why the
  # sentencing-ratio panel has no first sentence and a different
  # punitiveness. Each argument is one line (cap()). The ranking panel's
  # header says the ranking compares retributivists with all others; slide 5
  # and the paper's main text use the 453 who ranked deterrence or
  # incapacitation first, so the same measure has a larger d here
  # (essentialism 0.69 here, 0.59 on slide 5).
  labs(title = "Retributivists Under Four Groupings", x = "Cohen’s d", y = NULL,
       caption = cap(sprintf("Dark bars: one-sided p < .05 in the registered direction. Positive d: retributive side higher. 95%% CIs: about ±%s (±%s for thirds).",
                             HW_MAIN, HW_THIRD),
                     "The ratio is built from the sentences, so under it the first sentence is not run and punitiveness omits the sentence.")) +
  theme_hbar() +
  # TYPE SIZES. Row labels at 17 pt, large enough to read on a projector; with
  # no legend, its height goes to the rows, which is what lets 20 rows take
  # 17 pt without touching. The strips are 16 pt, because at 17 pt "Top vs
  # bottom third" and "Sentencing ratio" are clipped.
  # strip.clip = "off" lets a strip label run past its panel's edge rather
  # than be cut ("Ranking (vs all others)" is wider than its panel and runs
  # into the space on either side).
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK, size = 17),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
        # The tick labels sit 5 pt under the panel rather than the theme's
        # 9 pt; those 4 pt go to the gap above the caption (MARGINS, below),
        # so the rows keep their height. The theme sets this gap on
        # axis.text.x.bottom, which overrides any margin given to axis.text.x.
        axis.text.x.bottom = element_text(margin = margin(t = 5)),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 17, margin = margin(t = 4)),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", colour = INK, lineheight = 0.95,
                                  margin = margin(b = 2)),
        strip.clip = "off",
        panel.spacing.x = unit(1.6, "lines"),
        legend.position = "none",
        # MARGINS. The top margin is theme_slide()'s 26 pt, so the title
        # stands at the same height as on every other slide and does not jump
        # when Dan advances to this slide from slide 10. The bottom, left and
        # right margins are narrower than theme_slide()'s (10, 20 and 30 pt
        # against 18, 30 and 40), and the caption sits 8 pt below the axis
        # title rather than 16 (plot.caption below): that is the room that
        # lets 20 rows take 17-pt labels without touching. 8 pt, not less,
        # keeps the caption's first line further from "Cohen’s d" than from
        # its own second line, so it does not read as part of the axis title.
        # The caption's size, colour, centring and line height are
        # theme_slide()'s.
        # DANGER: restoring the bottom margin or the caption's 16-pt gap takes
        # the height from the rows, and descenders on one row label then
        # touch the capitals of the next (the gap is about 1 px now).
        plot.margin = margin(26, 30, 10, 20),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 14, colour = CAP_INK, hjust = 0.5,
                                    lineheight = 1.1, margin = margin(t = 8)),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 30, hjust = 0.5,
                                  margin = margin(b = 10)))
save_slide(fig06, "pt_06_four_groupings")
keep_values("pt_06_four_groupings", rbind(
  data.frame(
    label = sprintf("%s: %s (d, %d vs %d)", GROUPINGS$name[match(g6$grouping, GROUPINGS$key)],
                    ifelse(g6$variable == "punit_parts5z", "Punitiveness without the sentence",
                           as.character(g6$label)), g6$n1, g6$n2),
    value = g6$d, lower = g6$lower, upper = g6$upper, n = g6$n1 + g6$n2),
  # The dashed lines: each grouping's median absolute d (n = contrasts run).
  data.frame(label = paste0(GROUPINGS$name, ": median absolute d (dashed line)"),
             value = med6$median_abs_d, lower = NA, upper = NA,
             n = as.integer(table(factor(g6$grouping, levels = GROUPINGS$key)))),
  # The caption's "about ±": each grouping's median 95% CI half-width, unrounded
  # (the caption rounds it to two decimals).
  data.frame(label = paste0(GROUPINGS$name, ": median 95% CI half-width of d (caption, rounded to ",
                            hw6$shown, ")"),
             value = hw6$median_half_width, lower = NA, upper = NA,
             n = as.integer(table(factor(g6$grouping, levels = GROUPINGS$key))))))
fig06
```

```{r fig07_groupings_summary, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 7: ONE BAR PER GROUPING ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: for each registered grouping, the median of the
# absolute d across the registered contrasts it could run (20; 19 under the
# sentencing ratio), labelled with how many of them reached one-sided p < .05.
# The median is taken over ABSOLUTE d, as 01's scorecard and Table S16 take it
# ("Median absolute d"); under the three alternative groupings the shark's pain
# is negative, so the sign matters in principle; here the two medians are the
# same, because the negative d's all fall below the middle of each list.
# READS: g6 (slide 6); PAPER_scorecard.
# WRITES: pt_07_groupings_summary; its values.
# MATCHES: Supplement S5 and Table S16 (median d 0.51, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40;
#          one-sided p < .05 on 20, 15, 17 and 17); General Discussion,
#          Methodological Limitations (0.51; 0.20 to 0.40).
summ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(GROUPINGS$key, function(g) {
  x <- g6[g6$grouping == g, ]
  data.frame(grouping = g, n_run = nrow(x), n_sig = sum(x$p_dir < .05),
             median_abs_d = median(abs(x$d)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
# GUARDS: against 01's scorecard (the row set that counts punitiveness once,
# as the paper does), to 1e-8, and against the paper's printed values.
scc <- read_s2("PAPER_scorecard")
scc <- scc[scc$row_set == "Registered (H13 to H21), punitiveness once", ]
SC_RUN <- c(rank = "Ranking (primary)", med = "Median split", tert = "Tertiles",
            ratio = "Sentencing ratio grouping")
for (g in GROUPINGS$key) {
  s <- scc[scc$run == SC_RUN[[g]], ]; m <- summ[summ$grouping == g, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1, s$n_rows == m$n_run, s$n_one_sided_p05 == m$n_sig)
  same(m$median_abs_d, s$median_abs_estimate, paste("slide 7: median |d|,", g))
}
paper_same(summ$median_abs_d, c(0.51, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40), 2, "Table S16: median |d|")
stopifnot(identical(summ$n_sig, c(20L, 15L, 17L, 17L)),
          identical(summ$n_run, c(20L, 20L, 20L, 19L)))
# NOT PLOTTED, GUARDED FOR THE SPEAKER. The ranking's median here (0.51) is
# against all 577 others. Against the 453 deterrence- or incapacitation-first
# (slide 5's comparison and the paper's main text, Part 3) the same 20
# contrasts give a median of 0.41, with 19 of 20 at one-sided p < .05 (fear of
# crime falls short). A speaker who shows slides 5 and 7 together may be
# asked why the numbers differ; this is the answer, checked against the paper.
REG20 <- c(names(CONTRASTS), "punit_parts6")
cq20 <- cq[cq$variable %in% REG20, ]
stopifnot(nrow(cq20) == 20, setequal(cq20$variable, REG20),
          sum(cq20$p_dir < .05) == 19, cq20$variable[cq20$p_dir >= .05] == "fear")
paper_same(median(abs(cq20$d)), 0.41, 2, "Part 3: median d against the 453, 0.41")
paper_same(range(cq20$d), c(0.06, 0.66), 2, "Part 3: d from 0.06 to 0.66")

summ$panel <- factor(GROUP_TITLE[summ$grouping], levels = unname(GROUP_TITLE))
# The ranking, the registered primary grouping, in the darkest gray; the three
# alternatives in one lighter gray. The x labels name every bar.
# DANGER: not the lightest data gray (G4) for the alternatives. On slide 6,
# which comes just before this one, G4 means "one-sided p >= .05", and 15 of
# 20, 17 of 20 and 17 of 19 of the alternatives' contrasts are p < .05; in G4
# these bars would read as "not significant". G3 keeps the two kinds of bar
# clearly apart (#1a1a1a against #737373), as on slide 5.
# The count inside each bar is white on both grays: white on G1 is about 17
# to 1, and on G3 about 4.7 to 1, enough for the 17-pt count text. (Black on
# G3 would be only about 4.4 to 1.)
summ$shade <- ifelse(summ$grouping == "rank", "primary", "alternative")
fig07 <- ggplot(summ, aes(x = panel, y = median_abs_d, fill = shade)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  # The median above each bar ...
  geom_text(aes(y = median_abs_d + 0.012, label = fmt_d(median_abs_d)),
            vjust = 0, size = 8, fontface = "bold", colour = INK) +
  # ... and, inside it near the top, the count at one-sided p < .05, in white
  # on every bar (see the DANGER note above on the two grays).
  geom_text(aes(y = median_abs_d - 0.015,
                label = sprintf("%d of %d\nat p < .05", n_sig, n_run),
                colour = shade), vjust = 1, size = 6, lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(primary = G1, alternative = G3), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(primary = "white", alternative = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 0.6, 0.1), labels = axis_d,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.6), clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "Median Difference by Grouping", x = NULL, y = "Median Cohen’s d",
       # "Ranking: ... all 577 others" because the ranking's median here (0.51)
       # is against all others, the registered comparison; against the 453
       # deterrence- or incapacitation-first (slide 5, the paper's main text)
       # the median is 0.41.
       caption = cap("Bars: the median absolute Cohen’s d across the registered contrasts each grouping could run (20; 19 under the sentencing ratio).",
                     "Counts: contrasts reaching one-sided p < .05 in the registered direction. Ranking: retributivists vs all 577 others.")) +
  theme_vbar() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(colour = INK, size = 19, lineheight = 0.95))
save_slide(fig07, "pt_07_groupings_summary")
keep_values("pt_07_groupings_summary", rbind(
  data.frame(label = paste0(GROUPINGS$name, ": median absolute d"),
             value = summ$median_abs_d, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = summ$n_run),
  data.frame(label = paste0(GROUPINGS$name, ": contrasts at one-sided p < .05"),
             value = summ$n_sig, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = summ$n_run)))
fig07
```

# 7. Slides 8 to 11 and the main line of the talk

The recommended main line of the talk is slides 8, 9, 10 and 6. Slides 8 to
10 tell the story of slides 1 to 5 more plainly; slide 11 is a backup for questions about
whether revenge's lead over just deserts depends on how punitiveness is
measured.

```{r fig08_endorsing_punishing, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 8: ENDORSING AND PUNISHING ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: for revenge (four items), desert theory (five items)
# and the proportionality principle, two numbers side by side:
#   LEFT, "Endorse": the share of the 948 participants whose score is above the
#     neutral 4, with its exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval (share_cp());
#   RIGHT, "Go with punishing": the score's correlation with punitiveness
#     (the paper's six components), with its Fisher 95% interval.
# Read across a row, the slide sets what participants endorse against what
# goes with punishing. The proportionality principle is endorsed by most
# (83.1%) and goes with punitiveness hardly at all (r = .038); revenge is
# endorsed by about half and goes with punitiveness as closely as desert
# theory does.
# READS: sc (section 3); assoc (slide 2) and parts (slide 3), whose r's are
#        already guarded against the exports; H4_shares.
# WRITES: pt_08_endorsing_punishing (PNG, PDF, Docs copy); its values.
# MATCHES: Results, Part 2: H4 ("Most participants, 83.1%, agreed with the
#          proportionality principle"), H10 (revenge r = .676, desert theory
#          .674) and H6 (the principle, r = .038). NEW AND DESCRIPTIVE, not in
#          the paper: the shares agreeing with revenge (50.4%) and with desert
#          theory (89.5%); each is guarded against its value computed
#          independently of this document.
#
# "AGREE" MEANS A MEAN ABOVE THE NEUTRAL 4, the paper's rule for endorsement
# (H4's shares, and H12's "mean exceeded 4, the scale midpoint"). A score of
# exactly 4 is neutral, not agreement.
# DANGER: ">= 4" in place of "> 4" would count the neutral as agreeing and
# raise every share; the principle's share would then differ from the
# paper's 83.1%, and the guard below would stop the knit.
ROWS8 <- c(revenge = "Revenge (four items)", desert_theory = "Desert theory (five items)",
           proportionality_principle = "Proportionality principle")
sh8 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ROWS8), function(v)
  cbind(key = v, share_cp(sc[[v]] > 4), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
stopifnot(all(sh8$n == 948))

# GUARD: THE PRINCIPLE'S SHARE AGAINST THE EXPORT THAT GIVES IT. H4_shares
# counts the COMPLEMENT: the participants who do not endorse the principle
# (proportionality <= 4), 160 of 948. So the count endorsing must be 948 - 160,
# the share 1 minus the export's share, and the exact interval 1 minus the
# export's interval with its ends swapped (the Clopper-Pearson interval of
# (n - k) / n is exactly 1 minus that of k / n, reversed).
h4 <- read_s2("H4_shares")
h4p <- h4[grepl("^Do NOT endorse strict proportionality", h4$measure), ]
stopifnot(nrow(h4p) == 1, h4p$n == 948)
pp8 <- sh8[sh8$key == "proportionality_principle", ]
stopifnot(pp8$k == h4p$n - h4p$k, pp8$n == h4p$n)
same_each(c(pp8$share, pp8$lower, pp8$upper),
          c(1 - h4p$prop, 1 - h4p$ci_upper, 1 - h4p$ci_lower),
          "slide 8: principle's share against H4_shares",
          labels = c("share", "lower", "upper"))
paper_same(100 * pp8$share, 83.1, 1, "Part 2, H4: 83.1% agreed with the principle")
# GUARDS ON THE TWO NEW SHARES, against their values computed independently
# of this document (one decimal), and on the principle's interval.
paper_same(100 * unlist(sh8[sh8$key == "revenge", c("share", "lower", "upper")]),
           c(50.4, 47.2, 53.7), 1, "revenge: share agreeing 50.4% [47.2, 53.7] (new; computed independently)")
paper_same(100 * unlist(sh8[sh8$key == "desert_theory", c("share", "lower", "upper")]),
           c(89.5, 87.3, 91.3), 1, "desert theory: share agreeing 89.5% [87.3, 91.3] (new; computed independently)")
paper_same(100 * c(pp8$lower, pp8$upper), c(80.6, 85.5), 1,
           "principle: interval [80.6, 85.5]")

# THE CORRELATIONS, reused from slides 2 and 3 rather than recomputed, so the
# guards there (against PAPER_H10_cors and PAPER_H6, to 1e-8) cover them.
r8 <- rbind(assoc[assoc$key %in% c("revenge", "desert_theory"), c("key", "r", "lower", "upper", "n")],
            parts[parts$key == "proportionality_principle", c("key", "r", "lower", "upper", "n")])
stopifnot(identical(sort(r8$key), sort(names(ROWS8))), all(r8$n == 948))
paper_same(r8$r[r8$key == "revenge"], .676, 3, "slide 8: r(punitiveness, revenge) .676")
paper_same(r8$r[r8$key == "desert_theory"], .674, 3, "slide 8: r(punitiveness, desert theory) .674")
paper_same(r8$r[r8$key == "proportionality_principle"], .038, 3,
           "slide 8: r(punitiveness, principle) .038")

# ONE LONG TABLE FOR THE TWO PANELS. The left panel is in percent (0 to 100),
# the right in r; bar_facets() gives each panel its own axis (scales =
# "free_x"). txt is the printed value: shares to one decimal, as the paper
# prints 83.1%; r to three decimals, as slides 2 to 4 print it. tx places it
# just past the end of the interval, in each panel's own units (1.5 points of
# percent; .012 of r), and bar_facets() adds a space before the number, so
# it clears the interval's cap on any panel width.
# PANEL HEADERS in two lines: the panel's name, and under it what the
# panel's axis measures. The slide has no x-axis title, because the two
# panels measure different things; the second line of each header does that
# job. (On one line, "Go with punishing (r with punitiveness)" would run to
# the slide's right edge.)
P8 <- c(endorse = "Endorse\n(% agreeing)", punish = "Go with punishing\n(r with punitiveness)")
e8 <- data.frame(panel = P8[["endorse"]], key = sh8$key, value = 100 * sh8$share,
                 lower = 100 * sh8$lower, upper = 100 * sh8$upper, n = sh8$n,
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
e8$txt <- sprintf("%.1f%%", e8$value); e8$tx <- e8$upper + 1.5
g8 <- data.frame(panel = P8[["punish"]], key = r8$key, value = r8$r,
                 lower = r8$lower, upper = r8$upper, n = r8$n, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
g8$txt <- fmt_r(g8$value, digits = 3); g8$tx <- pmax(g8$upper, 0) + 0.012
d8 <- rbind(e8, g8)
d8$panel <- factor(d8$panel, levels = unname(P8))
# Revenge on top: rows are drawn bottom-up, so the levels are reversed.
d8$label <- factor(ROWS8[d8$key], levels = rev(unname(ROWS8)))
# FILL: revenge in G1 (with the white knock-out inside it); desert theory and
# the principle in the mid gray G3, not the light G4, which washes out on a
# projector. On G3 a black interval reads (about 4.4 to 1), so it stays black.
d8$shade <- ifelse(d8$key == "revenge", "Revenge", "Other")
FILLS8 <- c(Revenge = G1, Other = G3)
# EACH PANEL'S AXIS. The percent axis runs 0 to 100%, the whole scale, so a
# share is read against all participants. The r axis runs from -.06, so that
# the principle's interval, which dips below zero (-.026), is drawn whole, to
# .84, which leaves room for the printed .676. The breaks and labels are
# functions because the two panels need different ones: ggplot2 calls them
# once per panel, with that panel's limits and breaks.
lims8 <- data.frame(panel = factor(rep(unname(P8), each = 2), levels = unname(P8)),
                    x = c(0, 100, -0.06, 0.84))
brk8 <- function(lim) if (lim[2] > 2) seq(0, 100, 25) else seq(0, 0.8, 0.2)
lab8 <- function(x) if (any(x > 2, na.rm = TRUE)) ifelse(is.na(x), NA, paste0(x, "%")) else axis_r(x)

fig08 <- bar_facets(d8, FILLS8, lims8, breaks = brk8, labels = lab8, xlab = NULL,
                    scales = "free_x") +
  # The printed 89.5% runs past the 100% line into the space between the
  # panels; 3.4 lines (about 0.95 inches) keeps it clear of the right panel.
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(3.4, "lines"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK, size = 20),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", colour = INK,
                                  lineheight = 0.95, margin = margin(b = 10))) +
  # THE CAPTION: N; what "agree" means; which shares are new; and what
  # punitiveness is. Its components are grouped rather than listed ("two
  # punitive attitudes" are support for more punishment and rejection of
  # parsimony; "three policies" are three-strikes laws, life without parole
  # and the death penalty), because the full list pushes the caption to three
  # lines. Slides 2 and 9 use the same words; the six are listed in full
  # where punitiveness is read in (PUNITIVENESS, `scores` chunk).
  labs(title = "Endorsing and Punishing",
       caption = cap("N = 948. Agree: a mean above the neutral 4. The revenge and desert-theory shares are descriptive and not in the paper.",
                     "Punitiveness: six standardized components (two punitive attitudes, three policies, the first sentence). Error bars: 95% CIs."))
save_slide(fig08, "pt_08_endorsing_punishing")
keep_values("pt_08_endorsing_punishing", rbind(
  data.frame(label = paste("Agree (mean above 4), % of all, exact 95% CI:", ROWS8[e8$key]),
             value = e8$value, lower = e8$lower, upper = e8$upper, n = e8$n),
  data.frame(label = paste("r with punitiveness, whole sample:", ROWS8[g8$key]),
             value = g8$value, lower = g8$lower, upper = g8$upper, n = g8$n)))
fig08
```

```{r fig09_revenge_desert_both, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 9: REVENGE, DESERT, AND PUNITIVENESS, IN BOTH SAMPLES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: slides 2 and 4 merged into one slide of two panels,
# the whole sample and the retributivists, on one shared r axis, with the same
# four rows in the same order: revenge, desert theory, just deserts,
# severity-deserts. Nothing is recomputed: the values are slide 2's `assoc`
# and slide 4's `assoc4`, with every guard those chunks ran.
# READS: assoc (slide 2), assoc4 (slide 4).
# WRITES: pt_09_revenge_desert_both; its values.
# MATCHES: as slides 2 and 4: Results, Part 2, H10 (revenge .676, desert
#          theory .674, just deserts .432) and Part 3, H11 (revenge .570,
#          desert theory .545, just deserts .157). Severity-deserts (.734,
#          .558) is new and exploratory.
#
# WHO THE RETRIBUTIVISTS ARE, said in the right panel's header. Slide 9 is
# the first slide of the talk's main line (8, 9, 10, 6) that names the
# retributivists, and slides 10 and 6 name them only by their number, so the
# definition goes here, on the slide, rather than being left to the speaker:
# the participants who ranked retribution ("Criminals deserve to be
# punished") first of the four goals of punishment.
P9 <- c(whole  = sprintf("Whole sample (N = %d)", nrow(sc)),
        retrib = sprintf("Retributivists (n = %d)\nranked retribution first", nrow(rt)))
stopifnot(P9[["whole"]] == "Whole sample (N = 948)",
          P9[["retrib"]] == "Retributivists (n = 371)\nranked retribution first")
pick9 <- function(a, panel) data.frame(panel = panel, key = a$key, value = a$r,
                                       lower = a$lower, upper = a$upper, n = a$n,
                                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d9 <- rbind(pick9(assoc, P9[["whole"]]), pick9(assoc4, P9[["retrib"]]))
# GUARD: every row is the value slides 2 and 4 plot, in the right panel, to
# 1e-8 (a slip that swapped the two data frames would be caught here).
for (v in names(SCORES)) {
  same_each(unlist(d9[d9$panel == P9[["whole"]] & d9$key == v, c("value", "lower", "upper")]),
            unlist(assoc[assoc$key == v, c("r", "lower", "upper")]),
            paste("slide 9, whole sample:", v), labels = c("r", "lower", "upper"))
  same_each(unlist(d9[d9$panel == P9[["retrib"]] & d9$key == v, c("value", "lower", "upper")]),
            unlist(assoc4[assoc4$key == v, c("r", "lower", "upper")]),
            paste("slide 9, retributivists:", v), labels = c("r", "lower", "upper"))
}
stopifnot(nrow(d9) == 8, all(d9$n[d9$panel == P9[["whole"]]] == 948),
          all(d9$n[d9$panel == P9[["retrib"]]] == 371))
paper_same(d9$value, c(.676, .674, .432, .734, .570, .545, .157, .558), 3,
           "slide 9: the eight r's (paper; severity-deserts computed independently)")
d9$panel <- factor(d9$panel, levels = unname(P9))
d9$label <- factor(SCORES[d9$key], levels = rev(unname(SCORES)))
# FILL, as on slides 2 and 4: revenge G1 (white knock-out inside), desert
# theory and just deserts G3, severity-deserts WHITE with a black outline and
# a black interval (FAMILY_FILLS, section 3).
d9$shade <- unname(FAMILY[d9$key])
d9$txt <- fmt_r(d9$value, digits = 3); d9$tx <- pmax(d9$upper, 0) + 0.012

fig09 <- bar_facets(d9, FAMILY_FILLS, lims = data.frame(x = c(0, 0.84)),
                    breaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.2), labels = axis_r,
                    xlab = "Correlation with punitiveness (r)") +
  # The right panel's header is two lines (its name, then who the
  # retributivists are); the whole-sample header is one. vjust = 0 sets each
  # header on the bottom of its strip, so both headers end the same distance
  # above their bars and the right header's extra line rises above the left
  # one, rather than the one-line header floating halfway up its strip.
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(3, "lines"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", colour = INK, vjust = 0,
                                  lineheight = 0.95, margin = margin(b = 10))) +
  # The caption names the one new score by its bar, says what it is and that
  # it is new and exploratory, and defines punitiveness, whose components are
  # grouped as on slide 8 so the caption keeps to two lines.
  labs(title = "Revenge, Desert, and Punitiveness",
       caption = cap("Severity-deserts (white bar) averages desert theory and the severity index; it is new and exploratory. Error bars: 95% CIs.",
                     "Punitiveness: six standardized components (two punitive attitudes, three policies, the first sentence)."))
save_slide(fig09, "pt_09_revenge_desert_both")
keep_values("pt_09_revenge_desert_both", data.frame(
  label = paste0("r with punitiveness, ", ifelse(d9$panel == P9[["whole"]], "whole sample", "retributivists"),
                 ": ", SCORES[d9$key]),
  value = d9$value, lower = d9$lower, upper = d9$upper, n = d9$n))
fig09
```

```{r fig10_agency_shares, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 10: TWO MODELS OF AGENCY, IN SHARES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: slide 5 told in shares. For each of the seven measures
# on slide 5, two bars: the percentage of retributivists (371) who endorse it,
# that is, whose mean on it is above 4, the scale midpoint, and the same
# percentage among the participants who ranked deterrence or incapacitation
# first (453). The measures sit under the
# same two models of agency as on slide 5, with the same prediction in each
# group's header:
#   AGENCY AS BLAMEWORTHINESS (predicts retributivists higher): essentialism
#     about offenders, crime is a choice, rejecting society's responsibility;
#   AGENCY AS BENEVOLENCE (predicts retributivists no higher): hatred of
#     offenders, degradation of prisoners, infliction of suffering, harsh
#     prison conditions.
# Each difference between the two groups is also tested (share_diff():
# Newcombe's hybrid score interval for the difference, and the two-sample
# test of equal proportions without continuity correction). The tests are in
# the values table, not on the slide.
# READS: d (the measures), sc (the two groups); AGENCY and MODELS (slide 5);
#        H12_retributivist_endorsement and PAPER_H12_shares_vs_deter_incap.
# WRITES: pt_10_agency_shares; its values (each share with its exact 95%
#         interval; each difference in percentage points with its 95%
#         interval; each difference's two-sided p).
# MATCHES: Results, Part 3, H12 and Figure 11: the four hostility shares
#          (hatred 56.3% [51.1, 61.4] among retributivists; 36.2% among the
#          deterrence- or incapacitation-first), guarded exactly against the
#          exports behind Figure 11. NEW, not in the paper: the three
#          blameworthiness shares (guarded against their values computed
#          independently of this document) and all seven tests of the
#          differences.
# WHAT IS REGISTERED: the seven contrasts are preregistered as differences
# in means (H13, H16, H17, H19; the d's of slide 5). Among retributivists,
# the four hostility shares are H12's. The comparison of shares between the
# two groups is not registered (Table S22 note: the comparison groups'
# shares "were not registered, are descriptive"), nor is this comparison
# group, which leaves out the 124 who ranked rehabilitation first, nor the
# grouping into two models.
#
# "ABOVE 4" is the paper's rule for endorsing an attitude (Figure 11: "the
# percentage of participants whose mean exceeded 4, the scale midpoint").
# The slide says "endorsing" and "the scale midpoint", never "agreeing" or
# "the neutral 4": hatred is rated from "not at all" to "very much so", an
# intensity scale with no agree or neutral point (Table S22 note).
# DANGER: ">= 4" would count the midpoint as endorsing and break the guard
# against Figure 11's exports.
in_R  <- which(sc$grp_vs_deter_incap == "Retributivist")
in_DI <- which(sc$grp_vs_deter_incap == "Deterrence or incapacitation first")
stopifnot(length(in_R) == 371, length(in_DI) == 453,
          identical(in_R, which(sc$retributivist == 1)))
sh10 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(AGENCY)), function(i) {
  x <- d[[AGENCY$variable[i]]]
  # Every measure was answered by everyone in the two groups; a missing score
  # would silently drop out of a share, so the knit stops instead.
  stopifnot(!anyNA(x[c(in_R, in_DI)]))
  a <- share_cp(x[in_R] > 4); b <- share_cp(x[in_DI] > 4)
  df <- share_diff(a$k, a$n, b$k, b$n)
  data.frame(variable = AGENCY$variable[i], label = AGENCY$label[i], model = AGENCY$model[i],
             k1 = a$k, n1 = a$n, s1 = a$share, l1 = a$lower, u1 = a$upper,
             k2 = b$k, n2 = b$n, s2 = b$share, l2 = b$lower, u2 = b$upper,
             diff = df$diff, diff_lower = df$lower, diff_upper = df$upper,
             p_two = df$p_two, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

# GUARDS: THE FOUR HOSTILITY SHARES ARE THE PAPER'S (Figure 11), EXACTLY. The
# counts and group sizes must be identical, and each share and both ends of
# its exact interval must agree to 1e-8 with the export: retributivists from
# H12_retributivist_endorsement (H12), the deterrence- or incapacitation-first
# from PAPER_H12_shares_vs_deter_incap (the paper's descriptive comparison).
H12_ATT <- c(hatred = "Hatred toward offenders", degradation = "Degradation of prisoners",
             suffering = "Infliction of suffering", harsh = "Harsh prison conditions")
h12r <- read_s2("H12_retributivist_endorsement")
h12d <- read_s2("PAPER_H12_shares_vs_deter_incap")
for (v in names(H12_ATT)) {
  s  <- sh10[sh10$variable == v, ]
  er <- h12r[h12r$attitude == H12_ATT[[v]], ]
  ed <- h12d[h12d$attitude == H12_ATT[[v]], ]
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1, nrow(er) == 1, nrow(ed) == 1,
            s$k1 == er$k_endorsing, s$n1 == er$n, s$k2 == ed$k_endorsing, s$n2 == ed$n)
  same_each(c(s$s1, s$l1, s$u1, s$s2, s$l2, s$u2),
            c(er$share, er$share_ci_lower, er$share_ci_upper,
              ed$share, ed$share_ci_lower, ed$share_ci_upper),
            paste("slide 10 against Figure 11's exports:", v),
            labels = c("retributivists", "lower", "upper", "deterrence/incap.", "lower", "upper"))
}
# ... and against the paper's printed values (Part 3, H12).
paper_same(100 * unlist(sh10[sh10$variable == "hatred", c("s1", "l1", "u1")]),
           c(56.3, 51.1, 61.4), 1, "H12: hatred 56.3% [51.1, 61.4] among retributivists")
paper_same(100 * sh10$s2[sh10$variable == "hatred"], 36.2, 1,
           "H12: hatred 36.2% among the deterrence- or incapacitation-first")
# GUARDS ON ALL FOURTEEN SHARES against their values computed independently
# of this document, one decimal, in AGENCY's order.
paper_same(100 * sh10$s1, c(53.4, 74.7, 39.9, 56.3, 39.6, 46.6, 34.0), 1,
           "slide 10: retributivists' shares (computed independently)")
paper_same(100 * sh10$s2, c(33.3, 57.4, 21.9, 36.2, 23.8, 32.7, 16.6), 1,
           "slide 10: deterrence- or incapacitation-first shares (computed independently)")
# Every difference is positive: a larger share of retributivists endorses
# each of the seven, as the d's on slide 5 say (all one-sided p < .001 there).
stopifnot(all(sh10$diff > 0), all(sh10$diff_lower > 0))
print(data.frame(measure = sh10$label, R = round(100 * sh10$s1, 1), DI = round(100 * sh10$s2, 1),
                 diff = round(100 * sh10$diff, 1), lower = round(100 * sh10$diff_lower, 1),
                 upper = round(100 * sh10$diff_upper, 1), p_two = signif(sh10$p_two, 2)))

# THE PLOT DATA: one row per bar. The legend names both groups with their
# sizes, read from the data.
GRP10 <- c(R  = sprintf("Retributivists (n = %d)", length(in_R)),
           DI = sprintf("Deterrence or incapacitation first (n = %d)", length(in_DI)))
long10 <- rbind(data.frame(label = sh10$label, model = sh10$model, group = "R",
                           share = 100 * sh10$s1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
                data.frame(label = sh10$label, model = sh10$model, group = "DI",
                           share = 100 * sh10$s2, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
# DODGE ORDER. Dodged bars on a horizontal chart are placed bottom to top in
# the order of the group's levels, so "DI" comes first to put the
# retributivists' bar on TOP of each pair; the legend's order is set
# separately (breaks = below), retributivists first.
long10$group <- factor(long10$group, levels = c("DI", "R"))
long10$label <- factor(long10$label, levels = rev(AGENCY$label))
long10$model <- factor(long10$model, levels = unname(MODELS))
# WHERE EACH PRINTED SHARE STARTS: 1.2 points past the end of its bar.
# A LABEL ACROSS THE 50% LINE. A share from about 43% to just under 49% puts
# its printed value across the dashed line (here the retributivists' 47% for
# infliction of suffering), and the line would run through the number. Such a
# label gets a white box, just big enough to hide the line under the text
# (geom_label below). The label is not moved past the line instead, because
# a "47%" printed to the right of the 50% line looks, at a glance, like a
# share above half.
# LABEL_W10 is the width of a three-character label ("47%") at the 17-pt size
# below, in percentage points of this axis: the text measures about 0.46
# inches in the PNG, on an axis about 7.8 inches wide for 100 points, which is
# 5.8 points; 6 allows for the white box's padding. Only labels starting
# between 44 and 50 points are boxed, so every share from about 43% to just
# under 49% is covered.
# DANGER: the axis width depends on the side margins (theme(plot.margin) in
# the plot below). Widening them narrows the axis and makes each label span
# more points; re-measure the label and the axis and reset this value.
LABEL_W10 <- 6
long10$tx <- long10$share + 1.2
long10$straddle <- long10$tx < 50 & long10$tx + LABEL_W10 > 50
# GUARD: the white box is safe only where no other bar reaches it. Each pair
# of bars is retributivists on top, the other group below; the box of a
# retributivists' label sits between that measure's other bar (below) and the
# other group's bar of the measure above (drawn next up). Both must end
# before the label starts, or the box would cut a notch out of a bar; then
# the knit stops and the label needs another fix. A box on the LOWER bar of a
# pair would always cut into the retributivists' bar above it, which is
# longer on every measure, so only retributivists' labels may take a box.
box10 <- long10[long10$straddle, ]
LEVELS10 <- levels(long10$label)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(box10))) {
  m <- as.character(box10$label[i])
  stopifnot(box10$group[i] == "R")
  own_other <- long10$share[long10$label == m & long10$group == "DI"]
  above <- if (match(m, LEVELS10) < length(LEVELS10)) LEVELS10[match(m, LEVELS10) + 1] else NA
  above_other <- if (!is.na(above) &&
                     long10$model[long10$label == above][1] == box10$model[i])
    long10$share[long10$label == above & long10$group == "DI"] else -Inf
  stopifnot(own_other < box10$tx[i], above_other < box10$tx[i])
}
cat("Slide 10: labels boxed over the 50% line:",
    paste(box10$label, box10$group, collapse = "; "), "\n")

fig10 <- ggplot(long10, aes(x = share, y = label, fill = group)) +
  # THE 50% LINE, dashed, drawn FIRST so it sits behind the bars: it shows in
  # the gaps between bars and past their ends, where it lets the eye judge
  # which shares pass half, and it never runs over a bar or a printed value's
  # background (a line over the G3 bars, #737373, would vanish into them).
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", colour = MUTED, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.76) +
  # WHOLE PERCENTS at the end of each bar; the values table keeps the
  # decimals and the intervals. No interval is drawn: with two bars per
  # measure, fourteen whiskers and fourteen labels would crowd the slide, and
  # the tested quantity is the difference, which is in the values table.
  # Labels clear of the 50% line are plain text; a label across it (see the
  # guard above) is the same text in a white box with no border, drawn over
  # the line. The plain-text layer keeps EVERY row and prints "" for a boxed
  # one: position_dodge() places each bar's text by the pair it belongs to,
  # and a row dropped from the layer would leave its partner alone, centred
  # on the measure's row, on top of the other bar.
  # The boxed labels are placed by hand, for the same reason: with a dodge
  # width of 0.8 and two groups, the retributivists' bar is centred 0.2 above
  # the row.
  # DANGER: the 0.2 is tied to position_dodge(width = 0.8); change both
  # together.
  geom_text(aes(x = tx, label = ifelse(straddle, "", sprintf("%.0f%%", share)), group = group),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), hjust = 0, size = 6, colour = INK) +
  geom_label(data = function(k) k[k$straddle, ],
             aes(x = tx, label = sprintf("%.0f%%", share)), fill = "white",
             position = position_nudge(y = 0.2), hjust = 0, size = 6, colour = INK,
             label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.08, "lines"),
             label.r = unit(0, "lines")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = INK2, linewidth = 0.6) +
  # ONE PANEL PER MODEL, stacked, each as tall as its rows need, so the bars
  # are equally thick in both, as on slide 5.
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(R = G1, DI = G3), breaks = c("R", "DI"), labels = GRP10) +
  # The axis runs 0 to 100%, the whole of each group, with no padding, so the
  # bars start at the zero line.
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     expand = expansion(0)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100), clip = "off") +
  # "Share endorsing", as the paper's Figure 11 has it ("Participants
  # endorsing"); see "ABOVE 4" above for why not "agreeing".
  labs(title = "Two Models of Agency", x = "Share endorsing", y = NULL,
       # THE CAPTION, one line each:
       #   1. What a share is, in the paper's words (a mean above 4, the scale
       #      midpoint), and which shares are the paper's and which are new,
       #      named by the words in the two group headers, "benevolence" and
       #      "blameworthiness", so each can be matched to its panel.
       #   2. What was and was not preregistered. The seven contrasts were, as
       #      differences in means against ALL 577 other participants (the
       #      registered comparison; H13, H16, H17, H19). Three things on this
       #      slide were not: the comparison group (deterrence- or
       #      incapacitation-first only, the paper's stricter main-text
       #      comparison), the shares (Table S22 note), and the two-model
       #      grouping. Saying only "the seven contrasts are preregistered"
       #      would invite the reading that the share gaps drawn here are the
       #      registered tests.
       #   DANGER: this line names H13, H16, H17 and H19; the guard on slide 5
       #   (`ag`) is what ties those names to the export.
       #   Both lines are kept to about 125 characters, so that, like every
       #   other caption, they end at least 0.8 inches from the slide's edges.
       caption = cap("Share: percentage with a mean above 4, the scale midpoint. Benevolence shares are the paper’s (Figure 11); blameworthiness, new.",
                     "Preregistered as mean differences vs all 577 others (H13, H16, H17, H19); not this comparison group, the shares, or the grouping.")) +
  theme_hbar() +
  # SIDE MARGINS 24 pt wider than theme_slide()'s on both sides (54 and 64 pt
  # against 30 and 40). The axis ends at 100%, so the "100%" tick label is
  # centred on the panel's right edge and half of it sticks out; with the
  # usual 40 pt it ended a quarter of an inch from the slide's edge. The extra
  # room is added on BOTH sides so the title, legend and caption, which are
  # centred between the margins, stay centred where they are on every other
  # slide; widening the right margin alone would shift all three to the left.
  theme(plot.margin = margin(26, 64, 18, 54)) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", colour = INK, hjust = 0,
                                  margin = margin(t = 6, b = 8)),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(1.2, "lines"),
        # The legend centred on the slide, under the title, not over the panel.
        legend.location = "plot",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 19, colour = INK),
        legend.key.spacing.x = unit(18, "pt"),
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 4, 0))
save_slide(fig10, "pt_10_agency_shares")
# THE VALUES TABLE: each share (in percent) with its exact 95% interval; each
# difference (retributivists minus the deterrence- or incapacitation-first, in
# percentage points) with its Newcombe hybrid score 95% interval; and each
# difference's two-sided p (two-sample test of equal proportions, no
# continuity correction), in `value`, its interval columns left empty.
short10 <- sub(":.*", "", sh10$model)
keep_values("pt_10_agency_shares", rbind(
  data.frame(label = paste0(short10, ": ", sh10$label, ", % endorsing (mean > 4), retributivists, exact 95% CI"),
             value = 100 * sh10$s1, lower = 100 * sh10$l1, upper = 100 * sh10$u1, n = sh10$n1),
  data.frame(label = paste0(short10, ": ", sh10$label,
                            ", % endorsing (mean > 4), deterrence or incapacitation first, exact 95% CI"),
             value = 100 * sh10$s2, lower = 100 * sh10$l2, upper = 100 * sh10$u2, n = sh10$n2),
  data.frame(label = paste0(short10, ": ", sh10$label,
                            ", difference in percentage points (retributivists minus deterrence/incapacitation first), Newcombe hybrid score 95% CI"),
             value = 100 * sh10$diff, lower = 100 * sh10$diff_lower, upper = 100 * sh10$diff_upper,
             n = sh10$n1 + sh10$n2),
  data.frame(label = paste0(short10, ": ", sh10$label,
                            ", difference, two-sided p (two-sample test of proportions, no continuity correction)"),
             value = sh10$p_two, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = sh10$n1 + sh10$n2)))
fig10
```

```{r fig11_three_outcomes, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 11 (BACKUP): REVENGE AND DESERT, THREE WAYS ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: the correlations of five scores with three outcomes,
# as three panels side by side, with 95% intervals:
#   OUTCOMES (panels):
#     1. Punitiveness, the paper's six components;
#     2. Policy and sentence only: the mean of four of those six standardized
#        components, three-strikes laws, life without parole, the death
#        penalty and the first sentence. It leaves out support for more
#        punishment and rejection of parsimony, the two attitude components
#        whose wording is closest to the predictors (revenge's fourth item
#        asks for "punishing them more severely");
#     3. First sentence only: Sentence1_z, the first sentence standardized
#        within vignette.
#   SCORES (rows): revenge (four items), revenge on Study 1's three items
```
