```{r fig11_three_outcomes, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
#     (revenge_1 to _3, which leave out the fourth, harsher-punishment item),
#     desert theory, just deserts, severity-deserts.
# The slide answers the question whether revenge's lead over just deserts,
# and its tie with desert theory, depend on the attitude components of
# punitiveness. The tests are written to the tests table: in each panel,
# four-item revenge against desert theory, just deserts and severity-deserts
# (Steiger's Z, Zou's interval, two-sided).
# READS: d (the components, the revenge items, Sentence1_z); sc; ps (the
#        paper's punitiveness scores, for the guards); assoc (slide 2);
#        tests_a and TESTS (the tests chunk); PAPER_H10 (three-item revenge).
# WRITES: pt_11_three_outcomes; its values; six rows added to the tests table.
# MATCHES: in the first panel, the paper's revenge .676, desert theory .674
#          and just deserts .432 (Results, Part 2, H10), and revenge on
#          Study 1's three items, .549 (Supplement, Table S7, "three shared
#          items"). EVERYTHING ELSE IS NEW AND EXPLORATORY: severity-deserts,
#          and every correlation and test in the second and third panels.
#          Each is guarded against its value computed independently of this
#          document.
#
# THE SIX COMPONENTS, BUILT AS 01 BUILDS THEM (section 7.4, p5_parts and
# punit_parts6). Each component is the mean of its items, already
# reverse-coded so that high means more punitive; each is then standardized
# across the 948 and the six are averaged (01's zmean()). 01 applies its
# at-least-half rule to the two-item components (a mean of those who answered
# at least one of the two); every item was answered, so the rule changes
# nothing here, and the guard below says so.
# DANGER: the parsimony component must use parsimony_1_R and parsimony_2_R,
# the reversed items. The raw items would turn one component upside down, and
# the guard against the paper's punitiveness below would fail.
PART_ITEMS <- list(punish_more        = c("punishmore_1_R", "punishmore_2"),
                   parsimony_rejected = c("parsimony_1_R", "parsimony_2_R"),
                   three_strikes      = c("threestrikes_1", "threestrikes_2"),
                   life_without_parole = "LWOP",
                   death_penalty      = "deathpenalty",
                   first_sentence     = "Sentence1_z")
stopifnot(!anyNA(d[, unlist(PART_ITEMS)]))
parts11 <- as.data.frame(lapply(PART_ITEMS, function(cols) rowMeans(d[, cols, drop = FALSE])))
# STANDARDIZE EACH COMPONENT across the whole sample: scale() on the six
# columns at once standardizes each column on its own, exactly as zmean()
# does inside 01.
Z11 <- as.data.frame(scale(parts11))
# GUARDS: the six standardized components averaged reproduce the paper's
# punitiveness exactly (PAPER_person_scores$punit_six), and the five without
# the sentence reproduce the paper's five-component score (punit_five_z).
# Either failing would mean a component is built differently from 01's, and
# the policy-and-sentence score below could not be read as a part of the
# paper's punitiveness.
same(rowMeans(Z11), ps$punit_six, "slide 11: six components rebuilt = the paper's punitiveness")
same(rowMeans(Z11[, 1:5]), ps$punit_five_z,
     "slide 11: five components rebuilt = the paper's five-component score")
# POLICY AND SENTENCE ONLY (NEW, exploratory): the four behavioural components,
# each standardized as above, averaged. The two attitude components (support
# for more punishment, rejection of parsimony) are left out.
POLICY_PARTS <- c("three_strikes", "life_without_parole", "death_penalty", "first_sentence")
sc$punit_policy <- rowMeans(Z11[, POLICY_PARTS])
# FIRST SENTENCE ONLY: the within-vignette z-score as the data carry it (a
# correlation does not change when the sentence is restandardized).
sc$sentence1 <- d$Sentence1_z

OUT11 <- c(six      = "Punitiveness\n(six components)",
           policy   = "Policy and sentence only\n(four components)",
           sentence = "First sentence only")
OUT_COL <- c(six = "punit", policy = "punit_policy", sentence = "sentence1")
# ROW LABELS. Three-item revenge is labelled by its source, Study 1's three
# items (Table S7's "three shared items"). The Supplement also reports a
# three-item scoring without the father item (Table S12), which tracks
# punitiveness far more closely, and this slide's point is how much of
# revenge's lead rests on the fourth, harsher-punishment item, so the label
# must say which three items these are.
S11 <- c(revenge = "Revenge (four items)", revenge3 = "Revenge (Study 1’s three items)",
         desert_theory = "Desert theory", just_deserts = "Just deserts",
         severity_deserts = "Severity-deserts")
r11 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(OUT11), function(o)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(S11), function(s)
    cbind(outcome = o, key = s, cor_ci(sc[[OUT_COL[[o]]]], sc[[s]]),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))))
stopifnot(nrow(r11) == 15, all(r11$n == 948))
r11_at <- function(o, s) r11[r11$outcome == o & r11$key == s, ]

# GUARDS, FIRST PANEL: the four scores slide 2 plots are slide 2's values
# (themselves guarded against the exports), to 1e-8; three-item revenge is the
# r in PAPER_H10's three-item row (r_jk), to 1e-8, and the Supplement's .549.
for (s in names(SCORES))
  same_each(unlist(r11_at("six", s)[, c("r", "lower", "upper")]),
            unlist(assoc[assoc$key == s, c("r", "lower", "upper")]),
            paste("slide 11, punitiveness:", s), labels = c("r", "lower", "upper"))
h10_3 <- h10[h10$punitiveness == SIX & grepl("^one-sided.*three-item", h10$sidedness), ]
stopifnot(nrow(h10_3) == 1)
same(r11_at("six", "revenge3")$r, h10_3$r_jk, "slide 11: three-item revenge r (PAPER_H10)")
paper_same(r11_at("six", "revenge3")$r, .549, 3, "Table S7: three-item revenge .549")
# GUARDS, ALL FIFTEEN, against their values computed independently of this
# document, three decimals, in the order revenge four items, Study 1's three
# items, desert theory, just deserts, severity-deserts.
paper_same(r11$r[r11$outcome == "six"],      c(.676, .549, .674, .432, .734), 3, "slide 11: punitiveness r's")
paper_same(r11$r[r11$outcome == "policy"],   c(.628, .521, .621, .421, .659), 3, "slide 11: policy and sentence r's")
paper_same(r11$r[r11$outcome == "sentence"], c(.326, .268, .389, .299, .419), 3, "slide 11: first sentence r's")

# THE TESTS. In each panel, four-item revenge against desert theory, just
# deserts and severity-deserts: dep_cor() (Steiger's Z, Zou's interval), as
# for slides 2 and 4. In the first panel these three tests are ALREADY in the
# tests table (family A, whole sample, four-item revenge), with their
# registered-direction p's and guards; they are recomputed here only to show
# that they are the same tests, and only the six tests of the other two panels
# are added to the table.
RIV11 <- c("desert_theory", "just_deserts", "severity_deserts")
t11 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(OUT11), function(o)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(RIV11, function(h)
    cbind(outcome = o, rival_key = h,
          dep_cor(sc[[OUT_COL[[o]]]], sc$revenge, sc[[h]]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))))
t11_at <- function(o, h) t11[t11$outcome == o & t11$rival_key == h, ]
for (h in RIV11) {
  x <- t11_at("six", h); y <- tA("Whole sample", "revenge", h)
  same_each(c(x$diff, x$diff_lower, x$diff_upper, x$z, x$p_two),
            c(y$diff, y$diff_lower, y$diff_upper, y$z, y$p_two),
            paste("slide 11: first-panel test = tests table,", h),
            labels = c("difference", "lower", "upper", "Z", "p"))
}
# GUARDS against their values computed independently of this document. The
# differences are revenge minus the rival, so a rival that leads revenge gives
# a negative difference:
#   first sentence: desert theory leads revenge by .063 [.008, .119], p = .025
#     (two-sided p = .025478, which rounds to .025 and is guarded at three
#     decimals); revenge against just deserts .027 [-.041, .095], p = .44;
#   policy and sentence: severity-deserts leads revenge by .031 [-.009, .071],
#     p = .13.
a <- t11_at("sentence", "desert_theory")
paper_same(c(a$diff, a$diff_lower, a$diff_upper), c(-.063, -.119, -.008), 3,
           "first sentence: revenge minus desert theory -.063 [-.119, -.008]")
paper_same(a$p_two, .025, 3, "first sentence: revenge vs desert theory, p = .025")
a <- t11_at("sentence", "just_deserts")
paper_same(c(a$diff, a$diff_lower, a$diff_upper), c(.027, -.041, .095), 3,
           "first sentence: revenge minus just deserts .027 [-.041, .095]")
paper_same(a$p_two, .44, 2, "first sentence: revenge vs just deserts, p = .44")
a <- t11_at("policy", "severity_deserts")
paper_same(c(a$diff, a$diff_lower, a$diff_upper), c(-.031, -.071, .009), 3,
           "policy and sentence: revenge minus severity-deserts -.031 [-.071, .009]")
paper_same(a$p_two, .13, 2, "policy and sentence: revenge vs severity-deserts, p = .13")
print(data.frame(outcome = t11$outcome, rival = t11$rival_key, diff = round(t11$diff, 3),
                 lower = round(t11$diff_lower, 3), upper = round(t11$diff_upper, 3),
                 z = round(t11$z, 2), p_two = signif(t11$p_two, 3)))

# THE TESTS TABLE TAKES AN `outcome` COLUMN HERE, because with these rows it
# correlates revenge with three outcomes. The tests chunk's correlation rows
# are all on the paper's punitiveness; the endorsement rows (paired differences) have no
# outcome, so theirs is NA.
TESTS$outcome <- ifelse(grepl("^Correlation with punitiveness", TESTS$family),
                        "Punitiveness (six components)", NA_character_)
OUT_NAME <- c(policy = "Policy and sentence only (three strikes, life without parole, death penalty, first sentence; standardized, averaged)",
              sentence = "First sentence only (Sentence1_z)")
new11 <- t11[t11$outcome != "six", ]
# STATUS: every one of these rows is EXPLORATORY. H10 registered revenge
# against just deserts on punitiveness, one-sided; on another outcome it is
# not H10, so these rows are two-sided only and their one-sided column is NA,
# by the same rule as the severity-deserts rows (see the tests chunk).
out_c <- data.frame(family = "Correlation with another outcome: revenge vs rival (Steiger Z, Zou CI)",
                    sample = "Whole sample", revenge_scoring = REV_SCORING[["revenge"]],
                    rival = RIVALS[new11$rival_key], n = new11$n,
                    r_revenge = new11$r_revenge, r_rival = new11$r_rival,
                    r_revenge_rival = new11$r_revenge_rival,
                    M_rival = NA_real_, M_revenge = NA_real_,
                    difference = new11$diff, difference_lower = new11$diff_lower,
                    difference_upper = new11$diff_upper,
                    statistic = "Steiger Z", statistic_value = new11$z, df = NA_real_,
                    p_two_sided = new11$p_two, p_one_sided_registered_direction = NA_real_,
                    paired_d = NA_real_, paired_d_lower = NA_real_, paired_d_upper = NA_real_,
                    status = paste0("exploratory: outcome other than the paper's punitiveness ",
                                    "(slide 11, backup); reruns no registered test; two-sided only"),
                    outcome = OUT_NAME[new11$outcome], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
TESTS <- rbind(TESTS, out_c[, names(TESTS)])
TESTS <- TESTS[, c("family", "outcome", setdiff(names(TESTS), c("family", "outcome")))]
rownames(TESTS) <- NULL
# GUARDS on the grown table: six new rows, all two-sided only, none calling
# itself registered; every correlation row has an outcome.
stopifnot(nrow(out_c) == 6, nrow(TESTS) == 24,
          all(is.na(TESTS$p_one_sided_registered_direction[TESTS$family == out_c$family[1]])),
          !any(grepl("^registered test", TESTS$status)),
          !anyNA(TESTS$outcome[grepl("^Correlation", TESTS$family)]))

# THE PLOT. Rows bottom-up, so the levels are reversed; panels in OUT11's
# order.
d11 <- data.frame(panel = factor(OUT11[r11$outcome], levels = unname(OUT11)),
                  key = r11$key, value = r11$r, lower = r11$lower, upper = r11$upper,
                  n = r11$n, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d11$label <- factor(S11[d11$key], levels = rev(unname(S11)))
# FILL: four-item revenge G1 (white knock-out inside); three-item revenge
# HATCHED, white with dark stripes and a black outline, so it reads as a
# variant of revenge and is clearly not the same bar (G2 beside G1 is not
# clearly different on a projector); desert theory and just deserts G3;
# severity-deserts white with a black outline, as on slide 9.
SHADE11 <- c(revenge = "Revenge, four items", revenge3 = "Revenge, three items",
             desert_theory = "Desert", just_deserts = "Desert",
             severity_deserts = "Exploratory")
FILLS11 <- c("Revenge, four items" = G1, "Revenge, three items" = "white",
             Desert = G3, Exploratory = "white")
d11$shade <- unname(SHADE11[d11$key])
# The printed value starts .012 past the interval's end, as on slides 8 and
# 9, after the space bar_facets() puts before it, which keeps it clear of the
# cap on these narrower panels.
d11$txt <- fmt_r(d11$value, digits = 3); d11$tx <- pmax(d11$upper, 0) + 0.012

fig11 <- bar_facets(d11, FILLS11, lims = data.frame(x = c(0, 0.86)),
                    breaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.2), labels = axis_r,
                    xlab = "Correlation with each outcome (r)",
                    hatch = "Revenge, three items", hatch_run = 0.18, hatch_gap = 0.035) +
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(2.6, "lines"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 19, face = "bold", colour = INK,
                                  lineheight = 0.95, margin = margin(b = 10))) +
  labs(title = "Revenge and Desert, Three Ways",
       # THE CAPTION, one line each: which values are in the paper (the first
       # panel's revenge on both scorings, desert theory and just deserts;
       # revenge on Study 1's three items is in the Supplement, Table S7) and
       # that everything else is exploratory; and what "policy and sentence
       # only" contains.
       caption = cap("In the paper: the first panel’s revenge (both scorings; three items in Table S7), desert theory and just deserts. All else is exploratory.",
                     "Policy and sentence only: three strikes, life without parole, death penalty, first sentence (standardized, averaged)."))
save_slide(fig11, "pt_11_three_outcomes")
keep_values("pt_11_three_outcomes", data.frame(
  label = paste0("r with ", gsub("\n", " ", OUT11[r11$outcome]), ": ", S11[r11$key]),
  value = r11$r, lower = r11$lower, upper = r11$upper, n = r11$n))
fig11
```

# 8. Slides 12 to 14: desert and its limits, and the sentences

Two questions Dan asked about the paper's numbers. First, the paper gives
desert theory's correlations with the proportionality principle and the
severity index as .199 and .474 in one place and as .078 and .277 in another.
Both pairs are right: the first is the whole sample (Results, Part 2, H6),
the second the retributivists alone (Part 3, H11). Slide 12 shows the two
pairs side by side. Second, he asked for the sentences of the retributivists
and of the other participants. Slide 13 shows both sentences for the two
groups, and slide 14, a backup, splits the other participants by the goal
they ranked first.

```{r fig12_desert_limits_both, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 12: DESERT THEORY WITH ITS TWO LIMITS, IN BOTH SAMPLES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: the correlation of desert theory with each of two
# measures of how punishment should relate to the crime, in two panels, the
# whole sample and the 371 retributivists:
#   - the proportionality principle, the single item "Punishment should be
#     proportionate to the severity of the crime, no more and no less" (the
#     second part of just deserts);
#   - the severity index, the mean of "Punishment should be greater than the
#     seriousness of the crime" and, reversed, "Punishment should be less
#     severe than the harmfulness of the crime" (section 3).
# It answers Dan's question why the paper gives these two correlations as
# .199 and .474 in one place and .078 and .277 in another: the first pair is
# the whole sample (Results, Part 2, H6; General Discussion), the second the
# retributivists alone (Results, Part 3, H11; General Discussion). The same
# comparison is run in two samples.
# READS: sc and rt (sections 3 and 4); h6, PAPER_H6's rows (slide 3's
#        chunk); PAPER_H6_cors, PAPER_H11_H6, PAPER_H11_H6_steiger and
#        PAPER_reliability for the guards.
# WRITES: pt_12_desert_limits_both; its values, with the difference between
#         the two correlations in each sample (and its two-sided p), and the
#         SDs of desert theory, the principle and the severity index in each
#         sample.
# MATCHES: Results, Part 2, H6: r = .199 [.137, .260] with the principle and
#          .474 [.423, .522] with the severity index, ∆r = .275 [.193, .356],
#          Z = 6.53, two-sided p < .001 (correlations not registered).
#          Results, Part 3, H11 (Table S17): r = .277 against .078,
#          ∆r = .200 [.044, .352], two-sided p = .012. Table 1: desert theory
#          SD 1.19. NEW: the retributivists' SD of desert theory (0.83) and the
#          95% CIs of the retributivists' two r's, which the paper does not
#          print; each is guarded against its value computed independently of
#          this document.
#
# WHY THE RETRIBUTIVISTS' CORRELATIONS ARE LOWER, said in the caption. The
# retributivists were chosen for ranking "Criminals deserve to be punished"
# first, and their desert-theory scores bunch near the top of the scale (mean
# 6.13, SD 0.83, against SD 1.19 in the whole sample). A correlation depends
# on how much the scores vary: with less spread in desert theory, there is
# less for it to share with anything else. The caption says "partly", because
# the narrower spread is one reason and need not be the only one.

# PANEL HEADERS, one per sample, worded as on slide 9. This slide answers
# Dan's first question and may be shown on its own, without slide 9 before
# it, so the right header says who the retributivists are, as slide 9's does:
# the participants who ranked retribution ("Criminals deserve to be punished")
# first of the four goals of punishment. The caption has no room for this.
P12 <- c(whole  = sprintf("Whole sample (N = %d)", nrow(sc)),
         retrib = sprintf("Retributivists (n = %d)\nranked retribution first", nrow(rt)))
stopifnot(P12[["whole"]] == "Whole sample (N = 948)",
          P12[["retrib"]] == "Retributivists (n = 371)\nranked retribution first")
# ROW LABELS. The principle is on top, then the severity index, the order in
# which the paper names them. Each label carries a short gloss, so the caption
# need define only desert theory and the severity index's two items:
#   - the principle's gloss quotes the end of its item ("no more and no
#     less"), the words that make it a limit in both directions;
#   - the severity index's gloss is the Method's own reading of a high score
#     ("punishment at or above the offense and never below it", shortened).
# DANGER: do not gloss the index as "punishment greater than the crime"; its
# high end is punishment AT or above the offense (see slide 1's caption).
LIM12 <- c(proportionality_principle = "Proportionality principle\n(“no more and no less”)",
           severity_index            = "Severity index\n(at or above the offense)")
SAMP12 <- list(whole = sc, retrib = rt)
# One row per sample and measure: r of desert theory with the measure, its
# Fisher 95% interval and n (cor_ci(), section 2).
r12 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(SAMP12), function(s)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(LIM12), function(v)
    cbind(sample = s, key = v,
          cor_ci(SAMP12[[s]]$desert_theory, SAMP12[[s]][[v]]),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))))
r12_at <- function(s, v) r12[r12$sample == s & r12$key == v, ]
stopifnot(nrow(r12) == 4, all(r12$n[r12$sample == "whole"] == 948),
          all(r12$n[r12$sample == "retrib"] == 371))

# GUARDS, THE FOUR r's, against the export rows that hold them (1e-8, each
# number on its own): PAPER_H6_cors for the whole sample and PAPER_H11_H6 for
# the retributivists, where x is desert theory and y the limit.
h6c <- read_s2("PAPER_H6_cors"); h11h6 <- read_s2("PAPER_H11_H6")
EXP12 <- c(proportionality_principle = "Proportionality principle",
           severity_index = "Severity index")        # the exports' y labels
for (s in names(SAMP12)) for (v in names(LIM12)) {
  tab <- if (s == "whole") h6c else h11h6
  e <- tab[tab$x == "Desert theory" & tab$y == EXP12[[v]], ]
  stopifnot(nrow(e) == 1, e$n == r12_at(s, v)$n)
  same_each(unlist(r12_at(s, v)[, c("r", "lower", "upper")]),
            c(e$r, e$ci_lower, e$ci_upper),
            paste("slide 12:", s, v), labels = c("r", "lower", "upper"))
}
# ... then against the paper's printed values (three decimals). The paper
# prints the whole sample's intervals but not the retributivists'; those two
# are guarded against their values computed independently of this document.
paper_same(c(r12_at("whole", "proportionality_principle")$r, r12_at("whole", "severity_index")$r,
             r12_at("retrib", "proportionality_principle")$r, r12_at("retrib", "severity_index")$r),
           c(.199, .474, .078, .277), 3,
           "slide 12: desert theory with the principle and the index (H6 .199, .474; H11 .078, .277)")
paper_same(unlist(r12_at("whole", "proportionality_principle")[, c("lower", "upper")]),
           c(.137, .260), 3, "slide 12: whole sample, principle CI [.137, .260]")
paper_same(unlist(r12_at("whole", "severity_index")[, c("lower", "upper")]),
           c(.423, .522), 3, "slide 12: whole sample, severity index CI [.423, .522]")
paper_same(unlist(r12_at("retrib", "proportionality_principle")[, c("lower", "upper")]),
           c(-.024, .178), 3, "slide 12: retributivists, principle CI [-.024, .178] (new)")
paper_same(unlist(r12_at("retrib", "severity_index")[, c("lower", "upper")]),
           c(.180, .369), 3, "slide 12: retributivists, severity index CI [.180, .369] (new)")

# THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO CORRELATIONS in each sample, as the paper
# tests it: dep_cor() (section 2) with j = desert theory, the score both
# correlations share, k = the severity index and h = the principle, so the
# difference is r(desert, index) - r(desert, principle); Steiger's Z,
# two-sided, and Zou's interval. dep_cor() was written for revenge against a
# rival, so its columns are named for that use: here r_revenge is
# r(desert, index), r_rival is r(desert, principle), and r_revenge_rival is
# r(index, principle). Not drawn: it goes to the values table.
dr12 <- rbind(
  cbind(sample = "whole",  dep_cor(sc$desert_theory, sc$severity_index, sc$proportionality_principle)),
  cbind(sample = "retrib", dep_cor(rt$desert_theory, rt$severity_index, rt$proportionality_principle)))
# GUARDS against the exports: PAPER_H6's "Desert theory" row (whole sample)
# and PAPER_H11_H6_steiger (retributivists), where r_jk is the index and r_jh
# the principle, as here. Their p is cocor's two-sided p, which loses digits
# to cancellation once p is small (see same_p(), section 2), hence the floor.
h6d <- h6[h6$pair == "Desert theory", ]; h11s <- read_s2("PAPER_H11_H6_steiger")
stopifnot(nrow(h6d) == 1, nrow(h11s) == 1, h6d$n == 948, h11s$n == 371,
          h6d$alternative == "two.sided", h11s$alternative == "two.sided")
for (s in c("whole", "retrib")) {
  e <- if (s == "whole") h6d else h11s
  x <- dr12[dr12$sample == s, ]
  same_each(c(x$r_revenge, x$r_rival, x$r_revenge_rival, x$diff, x$diff_lower, x$diff_upper, x$z),
            c(e$r_jk, e$r_jh, e$r_kh, e$diff, e$diff_lower, e$diff_upper, e$z),
            paste("slide 12: difference,", s),
            labels = c("r(desert, index)", "r(desert, principle)", "r(index, principle)",
                       "difference", "lower", "upper", "Z"))
  same_p(x$p_two, e$p, paste("slide 12: difference p,", s), floor = 1e-15)
}
paper_same(unlist(dr12[dr12$sample == "whole", c("diff", "diff_lower", "diff_upper")]),
           c(.275, .193, .356), 3, "H6: ∆r = .275 [.193, .356]")
paper_same(dr12$z[dr12$sample == "whole"], 6.53, 2, "H6: Z = 6.53")
stopifnot(dr12$p_two[dr12$sample == "whole"] < .001)                # "p < .001"
paper_same(unlist(dr12[dr12$sample == "retrib", c("diff", "diff_lower", "diff_upper")]),
           c(.200, .044, .352), 3, "H11 (H6 among retributivists): ∆r = .200 [.044, .352]")
paper_same(dr12$p_two[dr12$sample == "retrib"], .012, 3, "H11 (H6 among retributivists): p = .012")

# THE SPREAD OF EACH SCORE in each sample (SD, n - 1 denominator). Desert
# theory's whole-sample SD is Table 1's (PAPER_reliability, 1e-8); the
# retributivists' SD is new, and both are guarded at the two decimals the
# caption prints. The SDs of the principle and the index go to the values
# table too, so a reader can see that their spread barely changes among
# retributivists (1.36 and 1.37; 1.24 and 1.13): the narrower spread is desert
# theory's.
sd12 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(SAMP12), function(s)
  data.frame(sample = s, key = c("desert_theory", names(LIM12)),
             sd = vapply(c("desert_theory", names(LIM12)),
                         function(v) stats::sd(SAMP12[[s]][[v]]), numeric(1)),
             n = nrow(SAMP12[[s]]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
sd_at <- function(s, v) sd12$sd[sd12$sample == s & sd12$key == v]
rel <- read_s2("PAPER_reliability")
rel_dt <- rel[grepl("^Desert theory \\(paper\\)", rel$score), ]
stopifnot(nrow(rel_dt) == 1)
same(sd_at("whole", "desert_theory"), rel_dt$SD, "slide 12: desert theory SD (PAPER_reliability, Table 1)")
paper_same(c(sd_at("whole", "desert_theory"), sd_at("retrib", "desert_theory")), c(1.19, 0.83), 2,
           "slide 12: desert theory SD, 1.19 whole sample and 0.83 retributivists")
paper_same(c(sd_at("whole", "proportionality_principle"), sd_at("retrib", "proportionality_principle"),
             sd_at("whole", "severity_index"), sd_at("retrib", "severity_index")),
           c(1.36, 1.37, 1.24, 1.13), 2, "slide 12: SDs of the principle and the index (new)")

# THE PLOT: bar_facets() (section 2), two panels on one shared r axis.
d12 <- data.frame(panel = factor(P12[r12$sample], levels = unname(P12)), key = r12$key,
                  value = r12$r, lower = r12$lower, upper = r12$upper, n = r12$n,
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d12$label <- factor(LIM12[d12$key], levels = rev(unname(LIM12)))   # principle on top
# FILL: the severity index in the darkest gray, G1, with the white knock-out
# inside its bar (mark_dark(), ci_knockout()); the principle in the mid gray,
# G3, with a plain black interval, which reads on G3 (section 2).
SHADE12 <- c(proportionality_principle = "Principle", severity_index = "Index")
FILLS12 <- c(Principle = G3, Index = G1)
d12$shade <- unname(SHADE12[d12$key])
d12$txt <- fmt_r(d12$value, digits = 3); d12$tx <- pmax(d12$upper, 0) + 0.012
# THE AXIS runs from just below zero, so the retributivists' interval for the
# principle (lower end -.024) is drawn whole, to .6, past the largest printed
# value; its ticks start at "0" (axis_r()).
fig12 <- bar_facets(d12, FILLS12, lims = data.frame(x = c(-0.05, 0.6)),
                    breaks = seq(0, 0.6, 0.2), labels = axis_r,
                    xlab = "Correlation with desert theory (r), with 95% CIs") +
  # The right panel's header is two lines, the left one line; as on slide 9,
  # vjust = 0 sets both headers on the bottom of their strips, so both end
  # the same distance above their bars.
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(3, "lines"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK, size = 19, lineheight = 0.95),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", colour = INK, vjust = 0,
                                  lineheight = 0.95, margin = margin(b = 10))) +
  # THE CAPTION: the severity index's two items on the first line, whole;
  # desert theory's definition and the reason the retributivists'
  # correlations are lower on the second ("0.83 vs. 1.19 overall": the
  # retributivists' SD against the whole sample's). The principle's gloss is
  # on its row, and the axis title says the error bars are 95% CIs, because
  # the two caption lines have no room left for it.
  labs(title = "Desert, Proportionality, and Severity",
       caption = cap("Severity index: “greater than the seriousness of the crime” and, reversed, “less severe than the harmfulness of the crime.”",
                     "Desert theory: five items. Retributivists’ correlations are lower partly because their desert scores vary less (SD 0.83 vs. 1.19 overall)."))
save_slide(fig12, "pt_12_desert_limits_both")
SNAME12 <- c(whole = "whole sample", retrib = "retributivists")
keep_values("pt_12_desert_limits_both", rbind(
  data.frame(label = paste0("r with desert theory, ", SNAME12[r12$sample], ": ",
                            EXP12[r12$key]),
             value = r12$r, lower = r12$lower, upper = r12$upper, n = r12$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("Difference, r(desert theory, severity index) minus r(desert theory, principle), ",
                            SNAME12[dr12$sample], " (Zou 95% CI)"),
             value = dr12$diff, lower = dr12$diff_lower, upper = dr12$diff_upper, n = dr12$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("Difference, ", SNAME12[dr12$sample],
                            ", two-sided p (Steiger Z)"),
             value = dr12$p_two, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = dr12$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("SD, ", SNAME12[sd12$sample], ": ",
                            c(desert_theory = "Desert theory", EXP12)[sd12$key]),
             value = sd12$sd, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = sd12$n)))
fig12
```

```{r fig13_sentences_groups, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 13: THE TWO SENTENCES, RETRIBUTIVISTS AND ALL OTHERS ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: the first and second sentences, in years (0 to 50,
# 50 = life), as violins, in two panels (first sentence, second sentence),
# each with two violins: the 371 retributivists and the 577 other
# participants, the registered ranking comparison. Each violin has every
# participant as a point, the mean with its 95% interval, and, under it, the
# median and the share choosing the 50-year maximum.
# READS: d (Sentence1, Sentence2, Sentence1_z); sc (grp_rank,
#        grp_vs_deter_incap); descriptives, PAPER_contrasts_rank,
#        PAPER_contrasts_vs_deter_incap and P3_sentence_direction_by_ranking
#        for the guards.
# WRITES: pt_13_sentences_groups; its values (means, intervals, medians, SDs,
#         shares choosing 50, the shares who reduced, kept, or raised the
#         sentence, and the two H14 d's).
# MATCHES: Results, Study 2: the whole sample's mean first sentence, 36.2
#          years, and the mean second sentence, 29.4. Results, Part 3, H14
#          (registered, on the first sentence standardized within vignette):
#          d = 0.51 against all others (Table S19) and 0.41 against the
#          deterrence- or incapacitation-first (Table S19, last column).
#          NEW AND DESCRIPTIVE: every number in years for the two groups (the
#          paper tests the standardized sentence, not raw years).
#
# WHY "ALL OTHER PARTICIPANTS" and not the deterrence- or incapacitation-first.
# Dan asked for retributivists and non-retributivists, and the registered H14
# comparison is with all 577 others (slides 6 and 7). The caption also gives
# the d against the stricter group, the comparison the main text reports.
# Slide 14 splits the 577 by the goal they ranked first.
# RAW YEARS. The three vignettes differ a little in their sentences, so H14 is
# tested on the sentence standardized within vignette. The slide shows raw
# years, which a talk audience reads directly; the vignettes were assigned
# at random and split almost evenly (315, 317, 316), so the groups'
# raw-year means are not distorted by vignette in any way that matters here,
# but they are descriptive, and the caption says so.

SENT13 <- c(Sentence1 = "First sentence", Sentence2 = "Second sentence")
GRP13  <- c(ret = "Retributivists", oth = "All other participants")
# THE GROUPS: the registered ranking grouping (grp_rank; section 3), first
# level "Retributivist". The guard ties it to the retributivist flag.
g13 <- ifelse(sc$grp_rank == levels(sc$grp_rank)[1], "ret", "oth")
stopifnot(!anyNA(d[, names(SENT13)]), !anyNA(g13),
          identical(g13 == "ret", d$retributivist == 1),
          identical(as.integer(table(factor(g13, levels = names(GRP13)))), c(371L, 577L)),
          all(unlist(d[, names(SENT13)]) %in% 0:50))   # whole years, 0 to 50

# ONE ROW PER SENTENCE AND GROUP: mean with its t interval (mean_ci()), the
# median, the SD, and the share choosing 50 with its exact interval
# (share_cp()). The median prints without decimals when it is a whole year.
sent_row <- function(x) {
  m <- mean_ci(x); s50 <- share_cp(x == 50)
  data.frame(n = m$n, mean = m$mean, lower = m$lower, upper = m$upper,
             median = stats::median(x), sd = stats::sd(x), k50 = s50$k,
             share50 = s50$share, share50_lower = s50$lower, share50_upper = s50$upper)
}
st13 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(SENT13), function(v)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(GRP13), function(g)
    cbind(sentence = v, group = g, sent_row(d[[v]][g13 == g]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))))
st_at <- function(v, g) st13[st13$sentence == v & st13$group == g, ]

# GUARDS.
# 1. The n's.
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(st13$n), c(371L, 577L, 371L, 577L)))
# 2. The whole sample's mean first sentence is the export's and the paper's
#    36.2, and the second sentence's the paper's 29.4; and each pair of group
#    means averages back to the whole-sample mean (n-weighted), which a slip
#    in the grouping would break.
desc <- read_s2("descriptives")
same(mean(d$Sentence1), desc$mean[desc$variable == "Sentence1"], "slide 13: mean first sentence (descriptives)")
paper_same(mean(d$Sentence1), 36.2, 1, "mean first sentence 36.2")
paper_same(mean(d$Sentence2), 29.4, 1, "mean second sentence 29.4")
for (v in names(SENT13))
  same((371 * st_at(v, "ret")$mean + 577 * st_at(v, "oth")$mean) / 948, mean(d[[v]]),
       paste("slide 13: group means average to the whole-sample mean,", v))
# 3. H14, the registered test, on the standardized first sentence: welch_d()
#    (section 2, 01's welch_contrast()) against all others (PAPER_contrasts_rank)
#    and against the deterrence- or incapacitation-first
#    (PAPER_contrasts_vs_deter_incap), 1e-8 for each number, then the printed
#    d's, 0.51 and 0.41.
h14 <- rbind(cbind(comparison = "all others",
                   welch_d(d$Sentence1_z, sc$grp_rank)),
             cbind(comparison = "deterrence- or incapacitation-first",
                   welch_d(d$Sentence1_z, sc$grp_vs_deter_incap)))
EXP14 <- list(read_s2("PAPER_contrasts_rank"), read_s2("PAPER_contrasts_vs_deter_incap"))
for (i in 1:2) {
  e <- EXP14[[i]][EXP14[[i]]$variable == "Sentence1_z", ]
  stopifnot(nrow(e) == 1, e$hypothesis == "H14", e$alternative == "greater",
            e$n1 == h14$n1[i], e$n2 == h14$n2[i])
  same_each(unlist(h14[i, c("M1", "M2", "t", "d", "lower", "upper")]),
            c(e$M1, e$M2, e$t, e$d, e$d_lower, e$d_upper),
            paste("slide 13: H14 against", h14$comparison[i]),
            labels = c("M1", "M2", "t", "d", "lower", "upper"))
  same_p(h14$p_dir[i], e$p_dir, paste("slide 13: H14 one-sided p against", h14$comparison[i]))
}
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(h14$n2), c(577L, 453L)))
paper_same(h14$d, c(0.51, 0.41), 2, "H14: d = 0.51 against all others, 0.41 against deterrence/incapacitation-first")
# 4. The raw-year values, against their values computed independently of this
#    document: first sentence 39.9 [38.8, 41.1], Mdn 45, 48.8% at 50, against
#    33.8 [32.7, 34.9], Mdn 30, 31.0%; second sentence 34.4 (Mdn 35) against
#    26.3 (Mdn 25).
paper_same(unlist(st_at("Sentence1", "ret")[, c("mean", "lower", "upper")]), c(39.9, 38.8, 41.1), 1,
           "first sentence, retributivists 39.9 [38.8, 41.1]")
paper_same(unlist(st_at("Sentence1", "oth")[, c("mean", "lower", "upper")]), c(33.8, 32.7, 34.9), 1,
           "first sentence, all others 33.8 [32.7, 34.9]")
paper_same(st13$mean[st13$sentence == "Sentence2"], c(34.4, 26.3), 1, "second sentence means 34.4 and 26.3")
# (== rather than identical(): the medians of whole-year sentences can come
# back as integers or doubles, and only their values matter.)
stopifnot(all(st13$median == c(45, 30, 35, 25)))
paper_same(100 * st13$share50[st13$sentence == "Sentence1"], c(48.8, 31.0), 1,
           "first sentence, share choosing 50: 48.8% and 31.0%")

# WHO REDUCED, KEPT, OR RAISED THE SENTENCE, by group. Values table only; the
# caption gives the share who reduced it.
# DANGER: THE ONE PARTICIPANT WHOSE FIRST SENTENCE WAS 0 is left out, as in
# the analysis (the sentencing ratio needs a first sentence above zero) and in
# the Supplement's figure of the groupings (Panel C, n = 947). The others'
# share who reduced is therefore 306 of 576, 53.1%. Counting that participant
# as having kept the sentence would give 306 of 577, 53.0%; the guard against
# P3_sentence_direction_by_ranking holds this document to the analysis's
# rule.
ok13  <- d$Sentence1 > 0
dir13 <- ifelse(d$Sentence2 < d$Sentence1, "reduced",
                ifelse(d$Sentence2 == d$Sentence1, "kept", "raised"))
DIRS  <- c("reduced", "kept", "raised")
tab13 <- table(factor(g13[ok13], levels = names(GRP13)), factor(dir13[ok13], levels = DIRS))
p3 <- read_s2("P3_sentence_direction_by_ranking")
EXP_GRP13 <- c(ret = "Retributivist", oth = "Other")       # the export's group names
for (g in names(GRP13)) {
  e <- p3[p3$group == EXP_GRP13[[g]], ]
  stopifnot(nrow(e) == 1, e$n == sum(tab13[g, ]),
            identical(as.integer(tab13[g, DIRS]), as.integer(unlist(e[, DIRS]))))
  same_each(tab13[g, DIRS] / sum(tab13[g, ]), unlist(e[, paste0("share_", DIRS)]),
            paste("slide 13: reduced / kept / raised shares,", g), labels = DIRS)
}
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(rowSums(tab13)), c(371L, 576L)))
paper_same(100 * tab13[, "reduced"] / rowSums(tab13), c(34.2, 53.1), 1,
           "reduced the sentence: 34.2% of retributivists, 53.1% of the 576 others")
dir_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(GRP13), function(g) do.call(rbind, lapply(DIRS, function(k)
  cbind(group = g, direction = k,
        share_cp(factor(dir13[ok13 & g13 == g], levels = DIRS) == k), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))))

# THE VIOLINS. A helper for slides 13 and 14, in the style of violin_1to7()
# (section 2): the violin is the shape of everyone's answers; each point is
# one participant, spread sideways only (seeded, so every knit draws the same
# slide); the black point is the mean and the black bar its 95% interval,
# with the mean printed beside it to one decimal.
#   long   one row per participant and violin: columns xlab (the violin's
#          axis label, a factor in the slide's order), years, and panel where
#          the slide has panels.
#   stats  one row per violin: xlab, mean, lower, upper (and panel).
# THE AXIS LABEL UNDER EACH VIOLIN carries the group, its n, the median, and
# the share choosing 50, so these sit under the violin they describe rather
# than in a legend. On slide 13 the two panels have different medians, so each
# panel's labels are its own levels, and the panels take scales = "free_x".
# scale = "width" gives every violin the same greatest width, as on slide 1,
# so a small group's violin is not drawn thinner for being small.
# adjust = 1.4 smooths the violins a little more than the default, because
# the sentences heap on multiples of 5 and the default bandwidth would draw a
# ripple for each heap.
# THE Y AXIS runs from 0 to 50 in steps of 10, with 50 labelled "50 (life)",
# as the instructions equated 50 years with life.
# DANGER: limits = c(0, 50) drops any value outside 0 to 50; there are none
# (guarded above), and a change to the data that produced one would silently
# lose it from the violins, so keep that guard with this scale.
violin_years <- function(long, stats) {
  ggplot(long, aes(x = xlab, y = years)) +
    geom_violin(fill = FILL_VIOLIN, colour = G3, linewidth = 0.6, width = 0.8,
                scale = "width", adjust = 1.4, trim = TRUE) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, seed = 1),
               size = 1.1, alpha = 0.3, colour = G3, stroke = 0) +
    geom_errorbar(data = stats, aes(x = xlab, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.1, linewidth = 1, colour = INK) +
    geom_point(data = stats, aes(x = xlab, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               size = 5, colour = INK) +
    geom_label(data = stats, aes(x = xlab, y = mean, label = sprintf("%.1f", mean)),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, nudge_x = 0.2, hjust = 0, size = 6,
               label.size = 0, fill = "white", label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines")) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 50, 10), limits = c(0, 50),
                       labels = c("0", "10", "20", "30", "40", "50 (life)")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Years in prison") +
    theme_vbar() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(colour = INK, size = 17, lineheight = 0.95))
}
# The median as printed: whole years without decimals ("45"), a half year
# with one ("25.5").
fmt_mdn <- function(m) ifelse(m == round(m), sprintf("%.0f", m), sprintf("%.1f", m))
# The label under a violin, four short lines: the group, its n, the median
# ("Mdn 45"), and the share choosing 50 ("48.8% chose 50").
# LINE BREAKS. The violins on slides 13 and 14 sit about 2.4 inches apart, and
# at 17 pt a line much wider than 2 inches runs into its neighbour's label.
# "Mdn 45; 48.8% chose 50" on one line is about 2.6 inches and did; split in
# two, the widest line ("All other participants", about 2.3 inches, on slide
# 13's narrower panels still clear of its neighbour) fits.
vlab <- function(name, s) sprintf("%s\n(n = %d)\nMdn %s\n%.1f%% chose 50",
                                  name, s$n, fmt_mdn(s$median), 100 * s$share50)

st13$xlab <- vlab(GRP13[st13$group], st13)
st13$panel <- factor(SENT13[st13$sentence], levels = unname(SENT13))
# Each panel's two labels, retributivists first (left), in panel order.
st13$xlab <- factor(st13$xlab, levels = st13$xlab)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(levels(st13$xlab)))
long13 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(st13)), function(i)
  data.frame(panel = st13$panel[i], xlab = st13$xlab[i],
             years = d[[st13$sentence[i]]][g13 == st13$group[i]])))
stopifnot(nrow(long13) == 2 * 948)

fig13 <- violin_years(long13, st13) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", colour = INK,
                                  margin = margin(b = 10)),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(3, "lines")) +
  # THE CAPTION: the registered test first, in the paper's terms (the d's are
  # on the standardized first sentence, not on the years drawn); then that
  # the years are descriptive, what the black marks are, and the share who
  # reduced the sentence. "vs." rather than "against" keeps the first line
  # within the 140 characters cap() allows.
  labs(title = "Sentences by Group",
       caption = cap("Registered test (H14), first sentence standardized within vignette: d = 0.51 vs. all others (0.41 vs. deterrence- or incapacitation-first).",
                     "Years are raw and descriptive. Black points: means with 95% CIs. Reduced the second sentence: 34.2% of retributivists, 53.1% of the others."))
save_slide(fig13, "pt_13_sentences_groups")
GNAME13 <- c(ret = "retributivists", oth = "all other participants")
SNAME13 <- c(Sentence1 = "first sentence", Sentence2 = "second sentence")
where13 <- paste0(SNAME13[st13$sentence], ", ", GNAME13[st13$group])
keep_values("pt_13_sentences_groups", rbind(
  data.frame(label = paste0("Mean (years, t 95% CI), ", where13),
             value = st13$mean, lower = st13$lower, upper = st13$upper, n = st13$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("Median (years), ", where13),
             value = st13$median, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = st13$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("SD (years), ", where13),
             value = st13$sd, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = st13$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("Share choosing 50 years (%, exact 95% CI), ", where13),
             value = 100 * st13$share50, lower = 100 * st13$share50_lower,
             upper = 100 * st13$share50_upper, n = st13$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("Share who ", dir_rows$direction, " the sentence (%, exact 95% CI; first sentence above 0), ",
                            GNAME13[dir_rows$group]),
             value = 100 * dir_rows$share, lower = 100 * dir_rows$lower,
             upper = 100 * dir_rows$upper, n = dir_rows$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("H14 (registered), Cohen's d, first sentence standardized within vignette, retributivists vs ",
                            h14$comparison),
             value = h14$d, lower = h14$lower, upper = h14$upper, n = h14$n1 + h14$n2)))
fig13
```

```{r fig14_sentences_by_goal, fig.width = 13.333, fig.height = 7.5}
# === SLIDE 14 (BACKUP): THE FIRST SENTENCE BY THE GOAL RANKED FIRST ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: the first sentence, in years, as four violins, one
# for each group defined by the goal of punishment ranked first of four:
# retribution (the retributivists, 371), incapacitation (266), deterrence
# (187) and rehabilitation (124), in that order, from the longest mean
# sentence to the shortest. Mean with its 95% interval, median, and share
# choosing 50, as on slide 13.
# It shows that the "non-retributivists" of slide 13 are not one group: the
# 124 who ranked rehabilitation first gave by far the shortest sentences, and
# the deterrence- and incapacitation-first sit between them and the
# retributivists.
# READS: d (Sentence1, Sentence1_z); `first` (section 3, the goal each
#        participant ranked first); st13 (slide 13); first_choice_group_means
#        for the guards.
# WRITES: pt_14_sentences_by_goal; its values.
# MATCHES: Table S20, "First sentence, z within vignette (H14)": 0.30, −0.14,
#          −0.06, −0.55 for retribution, deterrence, incapacitation and
#          rehabilitation first (standardized; the grouping by first choice
#          was not registered and no test compares the four groups). NEW AND
#          DESCRIPTIVE: every number in years.

# THE GROUPS, in the slide's order. `first` holds the column of the goal
# ranked first: 1 retribution, 2 deterrence, 3 incapacitation, 4
# rehabilitation (section 3). The slide's order is retribution,
# incapacitation, deterrence, rehabilitation.
# DANGER: the codes and the names must move together. GOAL14's names are the
# codes as character strings; the guard on the counts below catches a
# mismatch.
GOAL14 <- c("1" = "Retribution", "3" = "Incapacitation", "2" = "Deterrence",
            "4" = "Rehabilitation")
st14 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(GOAL14), function(k)
  cbind(code = as.integer(k), goal = GOAL14[[k]], sent_row(d$Sentence1[first == as.integer(k)]),
        z_mean = mean(d$Sentence1_z[first == as.integer(k)]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
stopifnot(identical(as.integer(st14$n), c(371L, 266L, 187L, 124L)))   # Part 3: 371, 266, 187, 124

# GUARDS.
# 1. The retribution-first group is slide 13's retributivists: the same mean,
#    interval, median, SD and share at 50, to 1e-8.
same_each(unlist(st14[1, c("n", "mean", "lower", "upper", "median", "sd", "share50")]),
          unlist(st_at("Sentence1", "ret")[, c("n", "mean", "lower", "upper", "median", "sd", "share50")]),
          "slide 14: retribution first = slide 13's retributivists",
          labels = c("n", "mean", "lower", "upper", "median", "sd", "share50"))
# 2. The four groups' standardized first sentence is Table S20's
#    (first_choice_group_means, H14 row, 1e-8 each), and the printed two
#    decimals. This ties the four groups to the paper's grouping.
fcm <- read_s2("first_choice_group_means")
fcm14 <- fcm[fcm$hypothesis == "H14" & fcm$outcome == "Sentence 1 (z within vignette)", ]
stopifnot(nrow(fcm14) == 1)
EXP_COL14 <- c("1" = "desert_first", "3" = "incapacitation_first", "2" = "deterrence_first",
               "4" = "rehabilitation_first")                   # in the slide's order
same_each(st14$z_mean, unlist(fcm14[, EXP_COL14]), "slide 14: standardized first sentence (Table S20)",
          labels = st14$goal)
paper_same(st14$z_mean, c(0.30, -0.06, -0.14, -0.55), 2, "Table S20: 0.30, −0.06, −0.14, −0.55")
# 3. The raw-year values, against their values computed independently of
#    this document: 39.9, 35.5, 34.5, 29.1; and the four groups' means
#    average back to the whole-sample mean (n-weighted).
paper_same(st14$mean, c(39.9, 35.5, 34.5, 29.1), 1, "first sentence by goal: 39.9, 35.5, 34.5, 29.1")
same(sum(st14$n * st14$mean) / 948, mean(d$Sentence1), "slide 14: group means average to the whole-sample mean")

st14$xlab <- factor(vlab(st14$goal, st14), levels = vlab(st14$goal, st14))
long14 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(st14)), function(i)
  data.frame(xlab = st14$xlab[i], years = d$Sentence1[first == st14$code[i]])))
stopifnot(nrow(long14) == 948)

fig14 <- violin_years(long14, st14) +
  labs(title = "First Sentence by First-Ranked Goal",
       caption = cap("Groups by the goal of punishment ranked first of four. Raw years, descriptive; no test compares the four groups.",
                     "Black points: means with 95% CIs. Table S20 gives the first sentence standardized within vignette for the same four groups."))
save_slide(fig14, "pt_14_sentences_by_goal")
keep_values("pt_14_sentences_by_goal", rbind(
  data.frame(label = paste0("Mean first sentence (years, t 95% CI), ranked first: ", st14$goal),
             value = st14$mean, lower = st14$lower, upper = st14$upper, n = st14$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("Median first sentence (years), ranked first: ", st14$goal),
             value = st14$median, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = st14$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("SD of first sentence (years), ranked first: ", st14$goal),
             value = st14$sd, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = st14$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("Share choosing 50 years (%, exact 95% CI), ranked first: ", st14$goal),
             value = 100 * st14$share50, lower = 100 * st14$share50_lower,
             upper = 100 * st14$share50_upper, n = st14$n),
  data.frame(label = paste0("Mean first sentence standardized within vignette (Table S20), ranked first: ", st14$goal),
             value = st14$z_mean, lower = NA, upper = NA, n = st14$n)))
fig14
```

# 9. What was written

```{r written}
# === THE TWO TABLES ===
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: writes every plotted value to one table, so a number on
# any slide can be looked up, and writes the tests behind slides 1 to 4, 9 and
# 11.
# WRITES: output/tables/princeton_talk_figure_values.csv (figure, label, value,
#         lower, upper, n), for all fourteen slides. Besides the plotted values
#         it holds slide 6's medians and typical interval half-widths,
#         slide 10's differences in percentage points and their two-sided p's
#         and slide 12's differences between correlations and their
#         two-sided p's (a p sits in `value`, with lower and upper empty; the
#         label says so), slide 12's SDs, and slides 13 and 14's medians, SDs,
#         shares choosing 50, who reduced, kept, or raised the sentence, the
#         H14 d's and Table S20's standardized means.
#         And output/tables/princeton_talk_tests.csv: the dependent-correlation
#         tests and paired endorsement differences of the tests chunk (18
#         rows) and slide 11's six tests on the other two outcomes, with an
#         `outcome` column saying which outcome each correlation test uses.
#         Slides 12 to 14 add no rows to the tests table.
# GUARDS: all fourteen slides' values are present, and nothing else.
vals <- do.call(rbind, VALUES)
rownames(vals) <- NULL
vals$label <- gsub("\n", " ", vals$label)
stopifnot(identical(names(vals), c("figure", "label", "value", "lower", "upper", "n")),
          identical(sort(unique(vals$figure)),
                    c("pt_01_endorsement", "pt_02_punitiveness", "pt_03_parts",
                      "pt_04_retributivists", "pt_05_agency", "pt_06_four_groupings",
                      "pt_07_groupings_summary", "pt_08_endorsing_punishing",
                      "pt_09_revenge_desert_both", "pt_10_agency_shares",
                      "pt_11_three_outcomes", "pt_12_desert_limits_both",
                      "pt_13_sentences_groups", "pt_14_sentences_by_goal")),
          !anyNA(vals$value))
write.csv(vals, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "princeton_talk_figure_values.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(TESTS, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "princeton_talk_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("%d plotted values written to princeton_talk_figure_values.csv\n", nrow(vals)))
cat(sprintf("%d tests written to princeton_talk_tests.csv\n", nrow(TESTS)))
print(list.files(OUT_FIGURES))
print(list.files(DOCS_FIG))
```
